la-unidad-latina-lambda-upsilon-lambda-f.name: La Unidad Latina, Lambda Upsilon Lambda Fraternity, Incorporated - Devastating Delta Chapter
la-unidad-latina-lambda-upsilon-lambda-f.description: La Unidad Latina, Lambda Upsilon Lambda Fraternity, Incorporated primarily seeks to take a student leadership role in meeting the needs of the Latino community through academic achievement, cultural awareness, community service, and promotion of the Latino culture and people. The Delta Chapter was Founded on April 24, 1988. It encompasses the University of Pennsylvania, Drexel University, Temple University, and Haverford College.
la-unidad-latina-lambda-upsilon-lambda-f.how_to_get_involved: Fill out our interest form and a current Hermano will get in contact with you.

the-disabled-coalition.name: The Disabled Coalition
the-disabled-coalition.description:
The Disabled Coalition seeks to create a safe space for the University of Pennsylvania’s disabled community to build authentic connections and support one another.
The space is designed by and for the disability community to serve as a platform to collaborate among students, faculty, and staff.
We aim to empower the disabled community on campus through education.
We support students with all types of disabilities, including mental and physical disabilities.
We stand in solidarity with students whose existence challenges institutional structures of oppression. 
We are open to all students who share an interest in disability.
the-disabled-coalition.how_to_get_involved: Attend any of our events! Everyone is welcome! Here is the link to our GroupMe: https://app.groupme.com/join_group/67915772/suMrjbOv

west-philadelphia-sanctuary.name: West Philadelphia Sanctuary
west-philadelphia-sanctuary.description:
West Philadelphia Sanctuary (WPS) works to strengthen social connection and belonging across West Philadelphia by creating welcoming, accessible spaces where people can gather, build relationships, and participate in community life.
Our team’s experience in community health across Philadelphia has shown us that many people experiencing loneliness, housing instability, or other social barriers lack consistent access to free, welcoming places to spend time with others and form lasting relationships. WPS responds by creating recurring community spaces centered on art, music, creative activities, and conversation, while connecting participants with essential resources and community-based support.
Through our weekly programs at The Rotunda and Walnut Street West Library, community partnerships, research, and program evaluation, we aim to understand what helps people build sustained social connection and translate those lessons into stronger programs across West Philadelphia. 
Apply: https://forms.gle/yFxfKp6xfMv5SRjp9
west-philadelphia-sanctuary.how_to_get_involved: Fill out this interest form! https://forms.gle/yFxfKp6xfMv5SRjp9

arts-house.name: Arts House Dance Company
arts-house.description:
Arts House Dance Company is a student-run dance company at the University of Pennsylvania. Arts House Dance Company [AHDC], founded in 1985, is known for its strong technique, innovative student choreography, vivid stage presence, and tight-knit family culture. The company performs contemporary, jazz, ballet, tap, and hip-hop at two annual shows, guest performances, and various campus events. AHDC is dedicated to presenting the highest level of performance and technique at Penn.
We're a tight-knit group of dancers from every background you can think of— we can't wait to dance with you!
arts-house.how_to_get_involved: Fill out this form if you are interested in auditioning in Fall 2026!

students-providing-aid-spaidupenn.name: Students Providing Aid (SPAid@PENN)
students-providing-aid-spaidupenn.description:
SPAid (Students Providing Aid) is a national organization dedicated to improving global health by empowering students to construct and distribute kid-friendly first aid kits to underserved communities. 
Vision: A healthier future by ensuring every child has access to essential first aid resources in underserved communities worldwide.
Mission: To address healthcare access gaps through collaboration, education, and strategic partnerships, making a tangible impact on global health. 
By joining our ambitious journey, you will not only become a part of the SPAid student organization at University of Pennsylvania, but also our growing community dedicated to making a real difference in global health. Together, we are not just distributing first aid kits; we are nurturing a global movement towards a more equitable healthcare landscape.
students-providing-aid-spaidupenn.how_to_get_involved:
Interested in joining SPAid? Please fill out the interest form to learn how you can make a difference today! https://forms.gle/CcNvrmxCmwoHUsj96
Membership into SPAid will be determined via an online application that indicates interest and potential commitment to the organization and a virtual interview with relevant SPAid officers assigned. 
Accepted General Body Members will be able to partake in all General Body Meetings as well as fundraising and volunteering events.

penn-ieee.name: IEEE@Penn
penn-ieee.description: IEEE@Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania and the University’s student branch of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE). We build community among students interested in electrical engineering, computer engineering, and related fields through networking and social programming, peer mentorship, academic support, and hands-on technical projects and competitions. We also advocate for students within the ESE department. All students are welcome, regardless of identity.
penn-ieee.how_to_get_involved:
Check out our website (https://ieee.seas.upenn.edu/) and make sure to sign up to be on the email list!
Follow us on Instagram: @penn_ieee

pfyd.name: Students for Youth Debate at Penn
pfyd.description:
We're a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. We strive to improve the educational outcomes of underprivileged students in Philadelphia. We work with students on their reading, writing, research, critical thinking, and public speaking skills.
Our volunteers are passionate about promoting educational justice and creating meaningful bonds with their students. 
We require no experience. If you would like to work in the speech and debate arm, we can train you.
We are non-competitive. We require no applications and no interviews. If you would like to volunteer with us, we will have a place for you in our organization and a community that you can rely on. 
We work around your schedule. Regardless of much time you can dedicate to SFYDP, we will have opportunities for you to stay engaged.

spec-jazz-grooves.name: SPEC Jazz & Grooves
spec-jazz-grooves.description: Jazz & Grooves is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that brings up-and-coming artists to Penn's campus throughout the year. Our shows are open to Penn students. Past talent includes Searows, Faye Webster, Perfume Genius, Moses Sumney, 100 gecs, Eartheater, SiR, Choker, Omar Apollo, Tierra Whack, Smino, and EARTHGANG, among others.
spec-jazz-grooves.how_to_get_involved: Join our weekly meetings where we discuss the good and the bad of the music world. Including, but not limited to: new album releases, listening parties, music hot takes, playlist swaps, J&G artists and shows we want to bring to Penn, and other events for the year. Updates will be sent through our GroupMe page and email list. Message jazzdirs@specevents.net to be added to the fam.

jewish-undergraduate-business-associatio.name: Jewish Undergraduate Business Association
jewish-undergraduate-business-associatio.description: The Jewish Undergraduate Business Association is committed to fostering a supportive community for Jewish students and their allies passionate about business and investing. Our mission is to connect like-minded individuals, provide professional development opportunities, and celebrate Jewish values within a business context.
jewish-undergraduate-business-associatio.how_to_get_involved: Apply via Penn Clubs or contact pennjuba@gmail.com

arab-student-dental-society.name: Arab Student Dental Society
arab-student-dental-society.description: Our mission is to introduce our heritage and culture to PDM students, and to promote oral health care and education to refugees, immigrants and most in need through interactive events and community service.

witg.name: Wharton Investment & Trading Group (WITG)
witg.description:
The Wharton Investment and Trading Group (WITG) is the premier undergraduate student group at Penn for professional preparation in finance-related careers. As a thriving hub of over 300 investment team members and 3,500 general members, WITG is the largest finance-oriented organization on campus. Our investment teams, Accelerator, and professional development programs teach the principles of value investing, business analysis, investment banking, and quantitative finance.
The WITG Accelerator is a semester-long educational program that gives underclassmen the opportunity to learn the fundamentals of investing, with no previous experience required. Students also have the opportunity to join investment teams, where upperclassman portfolio managers guide analysts through the process of pitching a stock — from sourcing, research, and valuation to effectively delivering a presentation. In addition to these programs, we partner with top Wall Street firms to provide WITG members with exclusive professional development opportunities, including career treks, networking sessions, and speaker events.

natives-at-penn.name: Natives at Penn (NAP)
natives-at-penn.description:
Natives at Penn (NAP) is Penn's Native student organization representing Native American, Native Hawaiian, Alaska Native, and Indigenous students, dedicated to increasing awareness of Native & Indigenous culture, history, and contemporary issues, while enhancing the visibility of Native & Indigenous students on campus, which is on Lenape Land. 
We:
Connect Native students, staff, alumni, and allies through events such as Penn's annual Powwow, our Indigenous Peoples' Day celebration, and other outings and activities that build cultural awareness and strengthen community
Advocate for more academic and professional resources, work with other intercultural groups to celebrate our intersectionalities, and host social gatherings that spark joy.
NAP is open to everyone! Whether you have been highly immersed in your culture, are still learning or wanting to learn more about your heritage, or don't identify as Native but want to be an ally, we are excited to welcome you all!
natives-at-penn.how_to_get_involved:
1) Register as a Club Member on Penn Clubs.
2) Complete our Member Registration Form: https://forms.gle/KADY5L24e76SgTfh9

csa.name: Chinese Students' Association (CSA)
csa.description:
The Chinese Students' Association (CSA) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that aims to promote social, cultural, and political Chinese and Chinese-American affairs to the community.
CSA exists to create an organization of individuals interested in these affairs and provide a way for all people to learn more about Chinese and Chinese-American culture, history, food, and news while creating a network and multifaceted family of members.
To carry out our mission, CSA holds numerous events including our annual cultural show production, holiday festivals, food events, trips, study breaks, and more.
csa.how_to_get_involved:
Anyone is welcome to come to our events and join our CSA family! Events are posted on our Instagram page. Add our Events Gcal: https://tinyurl.com/csagcal
If you are interested in joining on CSA Board, we are accepting FRESHMAN LIAISONS for our fall 2026 semester - come to SAC Fair to learn more about or visit our Instagram page to see how to apply!

penn-leads-the-vote.name: Penn Leads the Vote
penn-leads-the-vote.description: Penn Leads the Vote (PLTV) is Penn's only student-run, non-partisan program that increases voter engagement and voting while advancing Penn’s role of supporting the democratic and civic engagement of Penn students. PLTV is university-wide and its leadership comes from both the undergraduate and graduate student bodies of the University of Pennsylvania. During election cycles, PLTV connects the Penn community with the resources needed to register and check registration, to be informed, and to get out to the polls. Throughout the year, PLTV encourages students to learn about and engage with current issues and politics at the local, state, and national level.
penn-leads-the-vote.how_to_get_involved:
There are two ways to get involved with Penn Leads the Vote. We welcome everyone to join us regardless of your voter status and how much time you commit. There are opportunities for everyone! 
In order of least to most commitment: 
Volunteer: https://www.vote.upenn.edu/volunteer/
Job opportunities: https://www.vote.upenn.edu/job-opportunities/
Email us at pennvotes@upenn.edu or DM us on Instagram @pennvotes if you have any questions. We'd love to have you join us!
PS: are you registered to vote ?

hearts-for-the-homeless.name: Hearts for the Homeless Penn
hearts-for-the-homeless.description: Hearts for the Homeless (H4H) Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to improving the health and well-being of vulnerable populations in the local Philadelphia area through free mental and physical health screenings, education, and outreach opportunities for students who wish to contribute to our effort.
hearts-for-the-homeless.how_to_get_involved: Please email anyatal@sas.upenn.edu if you are interested in joining our organization!

sports-fitness-and-health-in-west-philad.name: Students at Penn for Sports Fitness and Health in West Philadelphia Schools
sports-fitness-and-health-in-west-philad.description: Are you a Penn student interested in making a difference and having fun while doing it? Are you passionate about health and wellness? Do you like sports and fitness? Do you enjoy volunteering and working with kids? If so, this is the place to be! Students at Penn for Sports, Fitness, and Health in West Philadelphia Schools brings Penn student volunteers together to create interest and involvement in sports, fitness, and health education among students in West Philadelphia. Join SFH, a student group at Penn, and get involved in schools in the West Philadelphia community to share your passion for Sports, Fitness, and Health!
sports-fitness-and-health-in-west-philad.how_to_get_involved: If you are interested in becoming a member of an incredible community of dedicated Penn students, fill out this form . If you have any questions about how to get involved or about the club and the programming we do, feel free to contact us.

penn-dems.name: Penn Democrats
penn-dems.description: Regarded as the largest club on the University of Pennslyvania’s campus, Penn Democrats is a student-run political organization open to all members of the Penn community – undergraduate and graduate alike. Our mission is to promote progressive political values on and off campus through dialogue and action. Penn Democrats seeks to engage and inform students across campus through regular speaker events, tabling on Locust Walk, and other educational opportunities. Whether you are interested in learning more about progressive issues or if you want to help inform more people about the issues you are passionate about, Penn Dems the activity to join!
penn-dems.how_to_get_involved: Anybody may join outside of usual recruitment times. All class years are welcome. Sign up for our weekly newsletter to keep up with announcements and current events: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1Hh0VG7TWUy9-rvZTha8dwK-TNX2KHPjqZhRzxZRI-QI/preview

ase-academy.name: Ase Academy
ase-academy.description:
Ase Academy is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania focused on mentorship and community engagement. Ase consists of Saturday sessions on Penn's campus between diverse undergraduate students and middle school students in the West Philadelphia. The program is partnered with Makuu and the Netter Center and is focused on providing supplemental educational support to our students. Since 1999, Ase mentors have provided students with academic and culturally enriching programming and the opportunity to learn on a college campus. 
Apply here: Ase Mentor Application 2025-26
ase-academy.how_to_get_involved: Apply: Ase Academy 2025- 2026 Mentor Application - Google Forms (feel free to reach out with any questions to upennase@gmail.com!)

government-politics-association.name: Government and Politics Association
government-politics-association.description: The Government and Politics Association is the largest student political organization at the University of Pennsylvania, devoted to all-partisan and balanced dialogue. The club aims to ever improve the culture of productive political discourse, education, and inquiry on Penn's campus.
government-politics-association.how_to_get_involved:
Anyone is free to attend GPA events, however we have opened up a new application for our Committees: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeSABtkrYdqObTycnbDy0IBiz_0Rimc_JTs_eoy6oin563eCA/viewform?usp=header
There are no membership requirements for Polybian, and there are brief application processes for PPR and Forum.
Interested in hearing more about GPA and its branches? Head to our website (penngpa.com) to join our listserv and check out our social media!
Our branches consist of the following:
Polybian Society - Open to all, weekly symposium discussions around a designated topic. It is a great way to meet new people and enjoy food and drinks 
Penn Political Union - Hosts events with student debates, faculty discussions, and prominent speaker events. All of these events are open to everyone and food is usually provided.
Penn Political Review - GPA's political publication branch. On top of its full-time editorial staff, students can also learn from the business side of publications 
Forum for Legislative Action - A legislative advocacy program where members write an original policy proposal and then meet with congressional staffers to get policy passed. A process that includes an annual trip to Washington, D.C. to lobby for the respective policies.

penn-neurosci.name: Neuroscience Society at Penn
penn-neurosci.description:
If you are curious about how the brain functions and how you can pursue a career in neuroscience or any related field, Neuroscience Society, a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania, is the perfect place for you! Join us for discussions, lectures, and workshops given by some of the world’s most prominent neurologists and neurosurgeons from the University.
We seek to bring together undergraduate and graduate students who share an avid interest in learning about the human brain and nervous system, potential academic and clinical careers in the field of neuroscience, and neurological disorders such as Parkinson’s disease and Alzheimer’s disease.
penn-neurosci.how_to_get_involved:
Neuroscience Society is an extremely welcoming and warm-hearted group of individuals, hosting many opportunities to get involved with neuroscience. New members can join and get involved beginning with our listserv, which you can join from this page! We offer two committees members can apply for: Journal and Research. Otherwise, you are welcome to join us at our general board meetings, speaker events, and physician shadowing events. Feel free to email us for more information or if you have any questions!
Our members also prioritize collaboration while seeking new opportunities of learning, whether it be through discussing articles in our Research Committee, ending in our yearly Research Committee Expo or contributing to our very own Neuroscience Society Journal under the Journal Committee.

pums.name: Society of Undergraduate Mathematicians @ Penn
pums.description: We are a student-run organization dedicated to promoting mathematics on Penn’s campus. We organize various events throughout the year to give students a taste of not only the theoretical aspect of math but also its various applications in life. No application required to join as a general member or come to our events!
pums.how_to_get_involved: Sign up for our mailing list if you want to stay updated on our programming.

alpfa.name: Association of Latino Professionals For America (ALPFA)
alpfa.description:
At Penn, Association of Latino Professionals For America (ALPFA) strives to help any undergraduate student of any major build their portfolio and learn what professionalism looks like. ALPFA is a per-semester long commitment with no business experience required. 
ALPFA was the first national Latino professional association in the United States, established in Los Angeles in 1972. ALPFA continues to build upon its legacy with a mission: To empower and develop Latino men and women as leaders of character for the nation, in every sector of the global economy.
For those looking to take their involvement to the next level, consider joining one of our committees focusing on event planning, marketing, or finance. This is an excellent way to gain leadership experience and directly impact our chapter's success. You can also participate in our mentorship program, either as a mentor or mentee, to connect with professionals in your field of interest.
alpfa.how_to_get_involved:
We're thrilled you're interested in joining the new ALPFA chapter at Penn! Getting involved is easy and rewarding. Start by attending our upcoming information session to learn about ALPFA's mission and the benefits of membership. Then, become an official member through our chapter website to access exclusive resources and networking opportunities. We encourage you to participate in our various events throughout the year, including professional development workshops, networking sessions with industry professionals, and community service activities.
Don't forget to follow us on social media to stay updated on chapter news and upcoming events. Ready to begin your ALPFA journey? 
Contact us at alpfa.upennchapter@gmail.com

penn-startup-initiative.name: Advanced Medicine & Healthcare Society (AMHS)
penn-startup-initiative.description:
The Advanced Medicine and Healthcare Society (AMHS) is dedicated to providing students with exceptional opportunities to engage with the forefront of medicine and healthcare. By leveraging Penn’s world-renowned hospitals and pioneering research institutes, AMHS connects students to unique resources and experiences that are rarely accessible at the undergraduate level.
Through programs such as physician shadowing, collaborations with leading healthcare and medical companies, and a novel student-run journal, members gain direct exposure to the latest advancements shaping patient care and clinical practice. AMHS fosters an environment where students can explore emerging technologies and engage with translational research efforts that are transforming healthcare today.
By integrating Penn’s unparalleled ecosystem into the undergraduate experience, AMHS equips its members with the knowledge essential to becoming future leaders in medicine and healthcare. Through these efforts, the society strives to empower students to contribute meaningfully to advancing the health and well-being of communities locally and globally.
penn-startup-initiative.how_to_get_involved: Please fill out this form to be added to our email chain: Interest Form

materials-science-and-engineering-societ.name: Materials Science and Engineering Society (MSE Society)
materials-science-and-engineering-societ.description:
The Materials Science and Engineering Society (MSE Society) is dedicated to bringing the materials science community at Penn together both inside and outside of the classroom.
The Materials Science and Engineering Society understands that a true education involves not only academic learning and technical skill sets, but also meaningful interpersonal interactions. We organize social events, lead academic workshops, and plan mentorship initiatives to promote professional growth in our student body. Additionally, we collaborate with faculty and administration of the Materials Science and Engineering Department to continuously improve the undergraduate experience in lecture-based classes, laboratory experiments, and co-curricular activities.
materials-science-and-engineering-societ.how_to_get_involved: If you're interested in joining our club, please email mseso@engineering.upenn.edu.

penn-carey-law-tennis-club.name: Penn Carey Law Tennis Club
penn-carey-law-tennis-club.description: We make tennis accessible and fun for everyone by providing an encouraging community to play, watch, or simply discuss tennis on campus. Whether you have never played tennis before and want a place to learn, played in college and want some match play, or just want to come with us to watch tennis, we would love to have you in our community!
penn-carey-law-tennis-club.how_to_get_involved: Please email Carson at the listed email to get involved!

vsa.name: Vietnamese Students' Association (VSA)
vsa.description:
The Vietnamese Students’ Association (VSA) is a student-led organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to promoting awareness and appreciation of Vietnamese and Vietnamese-American culture through community service, cultural performances, and social events.
VSA is committed to being an active member of both the Penn and greater Philadelphia communities while providing a welcoming space for Vietnamese students and anyone interested in Vietnamese culture to connect, build community, and celebrate their shared interests.
We welcome anyone interested in Vietnamese culture to join us! No application is required, and all of our events are open to everyone. Some highlights of Penn VSA include our annual Thanksgiving Potluck, ACE mentorship program, and Spring Culture Show.
vsa.how_to_get_involved:
Anyone is welcome to join VSA, whether you are interested in Vietnamese culture or just looking to meet new people!
Check out our Instagram @pennvsa for upcoming events!
To see all of our upcoming events or stay connected with us, check out our linkt.ree!

alzheimers-buddies.name: Alzheimer's Buddies
alzheimers-buddies.description: Alzheimer’s Buddies is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that pairs members with nursing home residents experiencing dementia in an attempt to alleviate the often-overlooked emotional and social challenges that stem from Alzheimer’s disease and related afflictions. Members visit their paired residents weekly and often develop close, meaningful relationships with them.
alzheimers-buddies.how_to_get_involved:
Applications for Fall 2026 will open on August 24th. 
Members are expected to visit their buddy at West Park Nursing Home or Atria Senior Living once a week for an hour, excluding certain weekends, such as fall/spring break, or after reading days. They are expected to attend bimonthly reflection meetings and participate in our guest lectures and fundraisers.
A member in good standing has done most, if not all, their weekly visits and attended most reflection meetings. While we host group visits every week for ease of transportation, we are also flexible to allow members to visit on their own time if the group visit time does not work! 
Link to Fall 2026 Application

southeast-asian-circle.name: Southeast Asian Circle at Penn (SEAC)
southeast-asian-circle.description:
Southeast Asian Circle at Penn (SEAC) immerses undergraduate students in the Southeast Asian business and cultural landscape for interested students at Penn.
Our organization has three main goals:
Share Southeast Asian cultures and customs with students through cultural events
Enrich the Southeast Asian business education of undergraduates 
Uplift Southeast Asian communities outside of Penn through volunteering and business consulting services
southeast-asian-circle.how_to_get_involved:
Club Structure
SEAC offers five Committees in Consulting, Finance, Professional Development, Marketing, and Member Engagement. From advising Southeast Asian American businesses to planning fun events, our Committees are the foundation to our organization.
Our Executive Board ensures that we are championing our values in every facet of our club. 
Executive Board/Committee Members
Must apply and interview at the beginning of the semester
Check media platforms of upennseac for links to informational sessions and to learn more about application details. 
Member Circle
No application is needed to be a General Body Member
Follow us on Instagram to know how to join our Group Me! @upennseac
Note: You do not have to identify as Southeast Asian to join. Open to all.

penn-india-association.name: Indian Association at Penn (IAP)
penn-india-association.description:
We intend to preserve and promote the Indian community at the University of Pennsylvania. All students irrespective of their background are welcome to join.
Our core objective is to serve as a strong cultural and support base for students. Our goals also include academic and professional support through greater alumni contact.
penn-india-association.how_to_get_involved: We are accepting of anyone who appreciates and enjoys Indian culture, ethics, values, and community. Fill in this Google form if you're interested in joining the club. Follow us on IG at indiaatpenn!

dc-law-club.name: Penn Carey Law DC Club
dc-law-club.description:
The Penn Carey Law DC Club unites members of the Penn Law community
who are interested in Washington, DC. We will have formal and informal events
to learn about the unique legal landscape in the DC area and to build a network
among peers and alumni in the region. The group is inclusive, creating spaces
to bring students together who are interested in life inside the Beltway and
navigating the myriad career opportunities available to lawyers in DC.

penn-kdsap.name: Kidney Disease Screening and Awareness Program (KDSAP) at Penn
penn-kdsap.description: Kidney Disease Screening and Awareness Program (KDSAP at Penn) at Penn is a student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania that provides free kidney health screenings and health education to underserved communities. We provide programs geared towards improving the health of underserved populations.
penn-kdsap.how_to_get_involved:
Members can volunteer at our monthly screenings, and in order to volunteer at a screening come to at least one clinical training session.
In addition to screenings, we have five committees engaged in initiatives for health education, professional development, marketing, community outreach, and screening operations. If you are interested in taking a leadership role in the organization, you can join our many committees as a deputy director. 
To learn more, join our email listserv and GroupMe: https://linktr.ee/pennkdsap

albanian-association-at-penn.name: Albanian Society at Penn
albanian-association-at-penn.description:
About Us:
Albanian Society at Penn is student club at the University of Pennsylvania of Students who hope to share various aspects of Albanian culture with the university community. All students interested in learning about Albanian culture, traditions, history and food are welcome to join. 
Goals:
Create a strong sense of the Albanian community at Penn
Serve as home-base of all college-based Albanian communities in the United States
Arrange open events in which accomplished Albanian speakers could come to Penn as guest lecturers
Strive for philanthropic events aimed towards facilitating conditions in our homelands
Collaborate with other Albanian communities in Ivy League universities
Strive for cultural exposition and general knowledge on Albanian History
Have pre-professional and cultural aspects
Create an inclusive, non-discriminatory environment
albanian-association-at-penn.how_to_get_involved:
Membership in our club is open year-round, and everyone is welcome to join! You can become a member by scanning the QR code on our Instagram page: https://www.instagram.com/penn_albanian_society/
Board elections are held annually.

pennmocktrial.name: Mock Trial at Penn
pennmocktrial.description:
Mock Trial is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania - and the school's one and only competitive mock trial program! Since 1996, the Mock Trial team has traveled around the country to compete in some of the most prestigious tournaments—providing outlets for future lawyers, actors, debaters, and public speakers to refine their craft. 
Mock Trial refers to the act of simulating a trial. It’s a mix of public speaking, acting and debating. It’s having the skill to take the stand and be a ridiculous eye-witness, a grieving mother or a serious doctor. It’s dominating the courtroom and swaying an entire jury box to vote in your favor. It’s sharp suits, fiery rebuttals, and fast paced objection battles.
pennmocktrial.how_to_get_involved:
Mock Trial at Penn is excited to be recruiting new members this fall! 
We will be tabling at the student activities fair on Locust during the first week of classes, and we’re excited to meet you all there! For anyone looking for a sneak peek at what life on PMT is like, we encourage you to attend our NSO preceptorial on Saturday, 8/22, in David Rittenhouse Laboratory. The location and signup information can be found in our Instagram bio.
We will be hosting 3 informational sessions during the first week of classes to provide an overview of our auditions process. You do not need to attend more than one info session—the content will be exactly the same on all three days! If you are unable to make our info sessions, please make sure to join our mailing list, as this is where our audition information and signup sheet will be circulated.
Our info sessions will take place in Houston Hall on Wednesday (8/26), Thursday (8/27), and Friday (8/28) during the first week of classes from 4:30-5:30 PM. Our Round 1 auditions will take place on the following Sunday (8/30). We will release information about audition logistics and signups at our info sessions!
You can follow our Instagram account, @upenn_mock_trial, to stay up to date with information about the team. Don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions!
PMT only recruits members in the fall semester. We do not take new members in the spring. 
Mailing list signup form linked HERE.
Instagram linked HERE.

mecha-de-penn.name: Movimiento Estudiantil Chicano de Aztlan (MEChA de Penn)
mecha-de-penn.description:
El Movimiento Estudiantil Chicana/o de Aztlán (MEChA is an organization that supports the exploration of Chicano culture, works to recruit Chicano students to Penn, and also works with the Penn community to build dialogue across campus and build a social consciousness within the Latino community.
MEChA is a student organization at Penn whose primary activities revolve around cultural exploration, not only around Chicano/Mexican-American culture, but Latina/o culture, Meso-American culture, history, and dialogue on issues varying from race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexuality, and many other areas. We continue working on campus to build dialogue and partnership throughout Penn’s campus.
mecha-de-penn.how_to_get_involved: Come to our events and GBMs!

wharton-graduate-association.name: Wharton Graduate Association
wharton-graduate-association.description: Our mission is to represent and advocate for student interests; build a cohesive and inclusive MBA community; and contribute to the improvement and development of The Wharton School.
wharton-graduate-association.how_to_get_involved: Membership is automatic for Wharton MBA students. Non-Wharton graduate students can join as well

pennsingers.name: Penn Singers Light Opera Company
pennsingers.description: Penn Singers Light Opera Company is a four-year student musical theatre company based at the University of Pennsylvania that values inclusivity of all genders, races, sexual orientations, and identities. We are a tight-knit community of performers, musicians, and technicians committed to producing top-notch musical theatre and having fun!
pennsingers.how_to_get_involved:
Come audition and/or interview to be a performing member, tech member or orchestra member in Penn's one and only four-year light opera company! Each semester, we welcome the next class of ‘Singers’, and we’d love to have you audition. Below you will find information on how to audition and interview for each of the three branches of singers: Tech, Orchestra, Performing. You are welcome to audition for more than one member status, but be sure to pay attention to the unique requirements of each!
----------------------
Performing Members:
How to Apply: Auditions will occur on August 29th (10am-12pm), August 30th (3pm-6:30pm), and August 31st (5pm-7pm) in Platt Performing Arts House. Your audition will only take approximately 15 minutes and you are welcome to come on any day. Please use the link below to sign up for an audition slot! We do also take walk-ins.
https://calendly.com/pennsingers/penn-singers-performing-auditions-clone
Audition Material: Please prepare to sing 32 bars (about 30 seconds) of a song in the musical theatre or classical/opera canon. You may sing acapella or with a backing track. Additionally, we will have you perform some scales and tonal recall exercises to do a vocal range test (no need to prepare anything for this). We are just trying to get an idea of your range and ability to recall notes. Lastly, we will ask you to perform a short acting side of your choice from a list of sides available in the audition waiting room. The side will not be expected to be memorized, so there is no need to prepare anything for this portion. We will additionally use this audition as a space for you to learn more about our company, ask any and all questions you may have and to gauge your personal fit with the company! 
**Auditions for Fall Show**
NOTE: Lead auditions for our Fall Show, will happen once admitted to the company. Only Performing Members in the company are allowed to audition for leads in our productions and every Singers Performing Member is guaranteed a role in all of our productions.
Auditions: Auditions will take place in-person and will be done in front of our professional Directors. Performing members auditioning for the show will be required to sing 32 bars of a song in the style of the show. You are welcome to use the same song you performed for New Member auditions as long as the song aligns with the genre of the show. After auditions, the Directors will schedule callbacks to take place that same week. This callback may include singing or reading from the show. All callback material will be sent to you in advance. 
---------------
Tech Members
Applicants are required to fill out an application and attend a chill, casual interview with our current Tech Directors. You will fill out your application at the interview! Interviews will be August 29th (10am-12pm), August 30th (3pm-6:30pm), and August 31st (6:30pm-8:30pm) in Platt Lobby at very similar times to perfrming auditions, so you can attend both if you would like.
Interviews are casual and last around 10 minutes; they give the Tech Directors a chance to understand where and how your interests can best fit our company. No experience is required to apply—we’d love to meet anyone interested in tech! Please email us at pennsingersvicepresident@gmail.com if you are to attend tech interviews! As always, please feel free to send any questions that you may have about interviews or Singers Tech to us as well. :)
--------------------
Orchestra Members 
How to apply and basic info: Auditions will be held on September 3rd from 4pm-8:30pm in Platt Performing Arts House (Platt 176). Walk-ins are welcome, but we prefer it if you sign up at the form which can be found at our instagram, @pennsingers. 
If there is a time conflict, please contact the Librarian and Orchestra Manager (LOM), Daniel Banstetter, at pennsingerslom@gmail.com before the deadline and we will work on a solution. 
Audition contents: The audition will consist of two sections: (1) instrument performance, and (2) an interview. 
For the instrument performance section, you will be required to perform one lyrical and one technical passage of music for about 30-60 seconds each*. The selections do not have to be from any particular genre. Please select what you feel will best express yourself as a musician! You may choose to audition on multiple instruments, which will occur within the same audition slot (though if necessary additional time accommodations can be made). Each instrument will require their own lyrical and technical passages. *Percussionist auditionees are exempt from the lyrical passage; please instead perform two separate technical passages.
For the interview section, which will occur after the instrument performance section, you will have a casual conversation with Dan following some guiding topic questions. 
If you are accepted you will have priority for parts in future shows as a member of the company! If you have any questions about orchestra or the requirements, you are welcome to contact Dan at pennsingerslom@gmail.com
--------------------
Penn Singers Light Opera Company is a four-year company. This means that once applicants are admitted into the organization, they do not have to interview or audition in the future. Performers will be asked to audition for the production’s professional director every semester, but their place in the company and in any production is always guaranteed. We perform a Broadway style musical in the Fall and a Light Opera in the Spring and all company members are expected to participate somehow in both semesters. We provide multiple ways to participate so that our members can adjust their commitments every semester depending on their workload while still being involved – in the production and socially – in the company.
The average time commitment for a Singers member varies depending on the branch. Performing members performing in our productions rehearse from 5-10 hours a week. Tech members are expected to work on tech from 2-4 hours a week. Orchestra rehearses 3-4 times before tech week (~5-8 hours in the semester before tech week). If someone would like to be a part of multiple branches, they have flexibility to choose which branch to be active in – and how active they want to be – every semester.
Penn Singers dues range from approximately $15-30 depending on your social commitment with the club. If dues pose any barrier to your involvement with the club, we are always able and willing to make arrangements so that anyone can be a part of Singers. 
If you have any withstanding questions, don't hesitate to reach out to us by email (pennsingers@gmail.com), or through our social media channels!

wharton-music-business-club.name: Music Business at Penn
wharton-music-business-club.description:
Music Business at Penn is the premier music business student organization at the University of Pennsylvania. We continually strive to give our members an exclusive educational experience through weekly meetings, immersive speaker events, concerts, peer-to-peer mentorship, internship recruitment events, and more.​
The Penn community believes in change starting at the root of powerful ideas. We enable our members to explore their creative abilities in the music industry while gaining inspiration from the personal connections they form with industry leaders and peers every semester.​
At the University of Pennsylvania, we also believe that change requires purpose-driven leaders. Given that music is one of the most rapidly accelerating industries in the world, our members are well-positioned to emerge as industry leaders in just a few years and meaningfully shape the world of music for the better.
wharton-music-business-club.how_to_get_involved: Check out our instagram @mbupenn for more details!

auxilium-tutoring.name: Auxilium Tutoring
auxilium-tutoring.description:
Auxilium (Latin translation: “support”) at the University of Pennsylvania is a student-run group that provides tutoring in partnership with the Cancer Support Community Greater Philadelphia and leads STEM sessions in collaboration with the Ronald McDonald House Charities of the Philadelphia Region. Auxilium serves the following children and teens:
those who have or are currently receiving medical treatment
those with loved ones, including siblings, parents, grandparents and/or guardians, receiving medical treatment
auxilium-tutoring.how_to_get_involved: To get involved, you can apply here. For more information, contact us at pennauxilium@gmail.com

hindu-yuva-at-upenn.name: Hindu YUVA at Penn
hindu-yuva-at-upenn.description:
Hindu YUVA at Penn exists to provide a venue for Hindus and non-Hindus alike to explore, celebrate, and discuss Hindu philosophy, scripture, and culture. The organization is committed to fostering discussion in the tradition of the Upanishads, where knowledge is most deeply understood and lived when it is subject to rigorous inquiry among well-intentioned interlocutors who are free to question, challenge, and build upon one another's understanding. 
We aim to represent the Hindu community at Penn with pride and care. This involves identifying where our community's values are consonant with the university's, celebrating our community's contributions to Penn, and advocating on behalf of Hindu students both on campus and beyond. The organization is further committed to seva (selfless service) in accordance with our tradition, directed toward our local community in ways most befitting the skills and capacities of our members.

upenn-hosa-future-health-professionals.name: HOSA @ Penn
upenn-hosa-future-health-professionals.description: HOSA@Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to empowering students to become leaders in the global health community through education, collaboration, and experiential learning. We strive to cultivate interdisciplinary understanding, promote public health awareness, and equip students with the knowledge, skills, and ethical foundations necessary to address health challenges at the local, national, and global levels. Through meaningful engagement and hands-on learning, HOSA@Penn aims to inspire a new generation of informed, compassionate, and effective health leaders.
upenn-hosa-future-health-professionals.how_to_get_involved: Fill out our interest form to get involved with HOSA!

asian-baptist-student-koinonia-for-under.name: Asian Baptist Student Koinonia (ABSK)
asian-baptist-student-koinonia-for-under.description: Asian Baptist Student Koinonia (ABSK) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania committed to studying the Word of God and building Christ-centered relationships as a family of God. We strive to learn more about God through the Bible and share God’s love with all in the Penn community.
asian-baptist-student-koinonia-for-under.how_to_get_involved:
Reach out via email (johnkims@sas.upenn.edu or hchang20@sas.upenn.edu) and check out our Instagram (@pennabsk)!
All are welcome to join us on Friday nights for thought-provoking Bible studies, food, fun and fellowship.
ABSK is a Christian fellowship ministering to college and university communities around the world.

pennplayers.name: Pennsylvania Players
pennplayers.description:
For over 85 years, the Pennsylvania Players have been bringing theater to the University of Pennsylvania. Since 1936, Penn Players has offered a creative outlet to a wide variety of students, including actors, singers, dancers, musicians, designers (scenic, lighting, costumes, properties), producers, stage managers, and others. With the guidance of professional directors (and musical directors for our musicals), Penn Players produces two major shows each year, a musical in the fall and a drama in the spring. Additionally, Players co-produces (with the other organizations of the Penn Theatre Arts Council) the student-directed One Acts festival in the winter to give student directors and playwrights a chance to gain experience.
Involvement with Penn Players is open to the entire University student community. All students (undergraduate, graduate, and LPS) are invited to audition, interview for staff/design positions, and participate in any of the production crews (sets, lights, costumes, running crews, etc.). All Penn students who have worked/are working on two Penn Players productions (or 1 + One Acts) are eligible to vote and run for the Penn Players Board of Governors during the next election. The Board is responsible for soliciting show proposals, choosing shows, hiring directors, and interviewing and selecting production staffs for all Penn Players productions. The Board also stays in contact with the Penn Players Alumni Club, keeps track of Penn Players membership, and creates and manages an annual budget.
Penn Players is a SAC (Student Activities Council) Funded Organization. We are a member of PAC (Performing Arts Council), and part of the TAC~E (Theater) division. SAC is part of OSL.
pennplayers.how_to_get_involved:
Performers – We hold auditions for our shows at the start of each semester. Auditions are laid back, and performers of any experience level are more than welcome. Auditions for our fall musical will take place September 1-2 from 6:30pm-10:30pm in Williams Hall. Send an email to pennplayers@gmail.com or tace.chair@gmail.com for more information! Can't wait to see you there!
Techies – Come out to tech interviews! These are very low-key interviews where you get to talk with our lovely tech team about your passion for theatre tech! We have both design and crew positions across all facets of tech, and people of any experience level are welcome. Interviews will take place September 7-8 from 6:30pm-10:30 pm in the Platt Student Performing Arts House Lobby. Looking forward to creating magic together!

penn-sports-analytics-group.name: Sports Analytics Group at Penn
penn-sports-analytics-group.description: The Sports Analytics Group at Penn (PSAG) is a student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to applying data-driven analysis to sports performance. Our mission is to foster a community of students passionate about leveraging statistical tools to provide actionable insights for Penn Athletics. Currently focused on basketball, baseball, and strength and conditioning, we collaborate closely with each coaching staff to identify key performance areas and develop methods for quantitative evaluation. Through predictive modeling, performance tracking, and clear data visualization, PSAG aims to enhance competitive advantage while deepening members’ understanding of sports analytics. By uniting students across disciplines, we seek to advance the use of analytics in athletic decision-making and prepare our members to become leaders in the application of data science to all fields.
penn-sports-analytics-group.how_to_get_involved: Request membership on Penn Clubs to join our email list and email pennsportsanalytics@gmail.com any questions.

penn-fimrc.name: FIMRC at Penn
penn-fimrc.description: FIMRC is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. Penn's Chapter of the Foundation of the International Medical Relief of Children works to help improve healthcare access for families around the world via sustainable healthcare community outreach programs and projects. It is perfect for a pre-health (or non-pre health, anyone can join!) student interested in international healthcare. Through FIMRC, you can participate in year-round club meetings and discussions, fundraising projects, our annual Adopt-a-Project, and even international volunteering trips!
penn-fimrc.how_to_get_involved:
Interested in joining FIMRC this year? Applications are currently open and are due Friday, September 25th at 11:59 PM!
Apply to FIMRC: Application Form
We post major event updates on our Instagram and also send newsletters via email. Stay up to date with FIMRC through the links below:
LinkTree/Email sign-up HERE

graduate-and-professional-student-assemb.name: Graduate and Professional Student Assembly (GAPSA)
graduate-and-professional-student-assemb.description: GAPSA is the official student government representing all 17,000+ graduate and professional students at the University of Pennsylvania. Our main functions are advocacy, programming, and funding for individuals and groups.
graduate-and-professional-student-assemb.how_to_get_involved:
If you are interested in joining GAPSA...
For Advocacy, please contact gapsa.advocacy@gapsa.upenn.edu. For Programming, please contact gapsa.programming@gapsa.upenn.edu. For funding, please contact gapsa.finance@gapsa.upenn.edu. For Operations, please contact gapsa.operations@gapsa.upenn.edu. Thank you!

ccc.name: Pediatric Childhood Cancer Coalition @Penn
ccc.description: Pediatric Childhood Cancer Coalition @Penn (PCCC) is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania that supports the childhood cancer community through service initiatives and advocacy. We represent a volunteer base of students dedicated to bettering the lives of children with cancer.
ccc.how_to_get_involved: Please fill out this quick form if you are interested in joining!

pennscience.name: Science Research Journals at Penn
pennscience.description:
Science Research Journals at Penn is a student group committed to promoting and raising the visibility of undergraduate and high school research. We were the first undergraduate student-led reserach journal in the country and continue to be the premier destination for top undergraduate and high school research, receiving hundreds of submissions per year.
We run two peer-reviewed journals: one showcasing high school research and another with undergraduate research. 
By creating a scientific forum for and by students, we hope to bring together young researchers, helping to make students feel that rather than participating in a disjointed and isolating endeavor, they are becoming a part of a true community of scholars. Throughout the year, we will host various research-related events internally and for the broader community.
pennscience.how_to_get_involved: Please subscribe to PennScience on Penn Clubs by pressing the bell icon (not bookmark) so we have your emails! Feel free to email us at pennscience@gmail.com if you have any questions as well.

university-of-pennsylvania-chamber-and-s.name: Penn Symphony Orchestra
university-of-pennsylvania-chamber-and-s.description: The Penn Symphony Orchestra was founded in 1878 and is comprised of musicians from throughout the University community, primarily non-music majors. Under the musical direction of Maestro Thomas Hong, this student ensemble rehearses three to four hours each week and performs a wide range of repertoire drawn from the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries. The Penn Symphony Orchestra rehearses and performs in historic Irvine Auditorium on Penn’s Campus.
university-of-pennsylvania-chamber-and-s.how_to_get_involved: Email our conductor (thomashongconductor@gmail.com) or check out our Instagram (@PennSymphony) for more information on our semesterly audition process.

the-wharton-equity-diversity-and-inclusi.name: Wharton Together
the-wharton-equity-diversity-and-inclusi.description:
About Wharton Together
We are a division-sponsored student group made up of Wharton undergraduates that connects students with the people, resources, and traditions that make Wharton feel like a community.
To do that, we run initiatives in two directions. We partner with administration across the division to make student-facing resources clearer, better publicized, and more usable. And we build community directly through programming: class year traditions, cross-class events, and spaces where students build deep connections. Through this work, we've been able to interface with faculty and administration on issues that shape student life and bring students together.
the-wharton-equity-diversity-and-inclusi.how_to_get_involved:
New members join a small board of 10-15 Wharton undergraduates who develop projects that impact the entire Wharton community.
As a board member, you gain skills in stakeholder engagement, policy implementation, and project development.
We strongly encourage first- and second-year Wharton students to apply if they care about student life and are interested in making a lasting impact on the community.

taiwanese-graduate-and-professional-stud.name: Taiwanese Student Association @ Penn
taiwanese-graduate-and-professional-stud.description: The Taiwanese Student Association (TSA) is a graduate student group at the University of Pennsylvania (Penn) dedicated to fostering community, cultural connection, and engagement around Taiwanese affairs among graduate and professional students and the broader Penn community. Through cultural, social, educational, and professional programming, TSA seeks to strengthen connections across Penn and promote an inclusive, connected campus community.
taiwanese-graduate-and-professional-stud.how_to_get_involved:
Please contact us via:
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/penntsa
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/upenntsa/

globemed-at-penn.name: GlobeMed at Penn
globemed-at-penn.description: GlobeMed is a network of university students passionate about global health and social justice, who work to improve the health of those living in poverty by forming multi-year partnerships with grassroots organizations across the globe. At the University of Pennsylvania, we bring the GlobeMed model of sustainable partnership and peer education to our members, our campus, and our local and global communities through issue-based awareness campaigns, fundraisers for our partner organization, local engagement and volunteering, and global health and social justice-related speakers and panels.
globemed-at-penn.how_to_get_involved: Email us at upenn@globemed.org so we can add you to the listserv and tell you more about our club!

student-nurses-at-penn.name: Student Nurses at Penn
student-nurses-at-penn.description:
SNAP is the School of Nursing’s oldest undergraduate student organization that is committed to creating programming and opportunities for nursing students. Our programming includes studying tips, career advice from SON faculty/classmates, tips on securing an externship, community service initiatives, community building events such as painting socials, wellness walks, and our annual Nursing Formal, and so much more! Enjoy free lunches and learn more about how to become active in the School of Nursing.
SNAP prides itself on being an organization that helps nursing undergraduates opportunities, resources, and platforms to develop leadership that will extend from the classroom, the hospital, and beyond.
student-nurses-at-penn.how_to_get_involved: Join our listserv and come to as little or as much as you would like! While there are perks to being an active member, all of our events are open to every undergraduate in the school of nursing. You can stay up to date with our events by joining our listserv (https://tinyurl.com/joinsnapfall24)!

business-industry-trends-bit.name: Business Industry Trends
business-industry-trends-bit.description: Business Industry Trends is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to educating and inspiring students interested in pursuing careers in business and entrepreneurship. Our goal is to provide a platform where members can connect with experienced professionals across a wide range of industries, gaining the insight and competitive edge needed to navigate the business world. We are committed to offering our members an immersive educational experience grounded in learning, mentorship, and professional growth.
business-industry-trends-bit.how_to_get_involved:
Applications for Committee Teams will take place at the start of Fall and Spring Semesters
To become a general body member, join our mailing list and provide basic information about yourself: https://forms.gle/HXhbScDpZvK6CVbr5

guatemala-health-initiative.name: Guatemala Health Initiative
guatemala-health-initiative.description:
The central goal of GHI is to put knowledge gained through participatory research and clinical and cultural experiences into developing effective, sustainable, and culturally sensitive health interventions/partnerships at Hospitalito Atitlán.
Our club is supported by Dr. Kent Bream, Associate Professor of Clinical Family Medicine and Community Health. The main enterprise of our club is a yearly summer trip to Hospitalito Atitlán, where undergraduates will support and expand the existing functions of Hospitalito Atitlán by raising funds, gathering medical supplies, and providing personnel support. In addition, students will have the opportunity to pursue their own independent projects in relation to epidemiology/population health studies. We will work during the year to appropriately train students for this trip, including cultural sensitivity training and workshops to gain basic clinical experience.
On campus, our club will be organized in a four-committee structure:
Projects Committee: The projects committee will focus on projects related to environmental sustainability in the context of medicine. Our projects committee will work to find common areas of waste in the medical setting and target efficient methods of waste removal. Potential topics include telehealth in Guatemala and setting up stations/access points for poorer patients to assist with patient outflow.
Research Methods Committee: In addition, training in epidemiological methods will be provided throughout the year through the Research Methods Committee; this will both guide students to select their own research methods and provide baseline training in this regard.
Conversations Committee: The Conversations Committee will work to set up events with guest lecturers from Perelmann, or faculty interested in the history of medicine, medical anthropology, or medical sociology.
Finance and Operations Committee: The Finance and Operations Committee will work to both secure funding sources for the Guatemala trip and manage our monetary investments.
Overall, the undergraduate branch of GHI, supported by faculty at the Perelman School of Medicine, aims to develop sustainable health interventions at Hospitalito Atitlán in Guatemala. Our club will raise funds, provide medical supplies and support, and pursue epidemiology projects, with training in cultural sensitivity and clinical skills.
guatemala-health-initiative.how_to_get_involved: Reach out to Anna Mueller and Nitin Seshadri at annagm@sas.upenn.edu and nitin25@sas.upenn.edu for updates about future events!

penn-environmental-group.name: Environmental Group at Penn (PEG)
penn-environmental-group.description: The Environmental Group at Penn (PEG) is a broad-interest student group that focuses on a combination of events, speakers, and projects dedicated to enhancing the environmental community at Penn and working toward a greener future. PEG was founded in 1971 by students who were actively involved in the 1970 Earth Day celebration.
penn-environmental-group.how_to_get_involved:
We always welcome new members! Please join our listserv at http://eepurl.com/EWCT1 or email pennvironmentalgroup@gmail.com for fall semester meeting dates and information.
Apply Here: https://forms.gle/f14d3HqQmdBtXyXv9

be-body-positive-upenn.name: Body Empowerment Project at Penn
be-body-positive-upenn.description:
Body Empowerment Project at Penn is a student group focused on addressing eating disorder risk among Penn students through an original curriculum led by trained Penn volunteers. The program helps participants develop a more balanced and accepting relationship with their bodies through a weight-neutral and health-centered approach. Participants acquire tools and strategies to live intuitively, develop self-love, expand their definition of beauty, and build a strong community of support.
Our group holds 3 events per month: a "pop-up" workshop with another student organization, a fun, self-empowering event including but not limited to pumpkin painting and puppy dog yoga, and a consistent GBM centered around small group discussion and peer-to-peer education. Our goal is to establish a cohort of facilitators to run a 10-week education program.
BEP is a safe space for to feel supported and loved as they are. We would love for you to join our community!
be-body-positive-upenn.how_to_get_involved: Reach out via email OR apply via link (coming in mid Sep)

penn-ballet.name: Ballet at Penn
penn-ballet.description: Ballet at Penn, formerly Penn Ballet, is a student-run organization created to allow dancers of any level at the University of Pennsylvania to share their love of classical ballet despite demanding academic commitments. We are the only student group at Penn dedicated to ballet. The Performance Company is an audition-based community of experienced dancers who love learning, teaching, and performing classical and contemporary ballet repertoire. The Company rehearses regularly to put together a show for a large audience of friends and family each semester. Members of the Company help those without much ballet experience to discover the art form, supporting them in furthering their technique and performance quality through our free weekly open classes. We invite all Penn students to be part of our ballet community and create art together.
penn-ballet.how_to_get_involved: All undergraduate and graduate students are welcome to attend our open classes and audition for the performance company. Please send us an email (pennballet10@gmail.com) to be added to our listserv for updates on all of our 2026 events!

phi-delta-epsilon.name: Phi Delta Epsilon
phi-delta-epsilon.description:
What is Phi Delta Epsilon?
Phi Delta Epsilon International Medical Fraternity creates physicians of integrity with a lifelong commitment to our guiding principles of philanthropy, deity, and education through fellowship, service, mentoring, and leadership. We have a chapter of around 80 members with diverse backgrounds and interests. 
What We Do
In our chapter, we strive to foster a community of pre-med students through a variety of social, service, philanthropy, and educational events. We pride ourselves for our balance between social and professional development programming. We are a tight-knit family, where members are consistently looking out for and supporting one another. Additionally, we provide professional development opportunities to ensure that our members are positioned to succeed as pre-medical students.
Who Can Join
Any undergraduate student at the University of Pennsylvania intending on pursuing a degree in medicine (M.D. or D.O.) is encouraged to join. We are a co-ed pre-professional fraternity.
phi-delta-epsilon.how_to_get_involved: We recruit at the start of every semester. Please visit our website at upennphide.com for more details! Our Instagram page will also post more information about recruitment closer to the start of each semester!

mno.name: Minorities in Nursing Organization
mno.description:
Founded in 2001, Minorities in Nursing Organization is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania formed with the mission of promoting cultural awareness within the School of Nursing and the University at large. Regardless of age, race, ethnicity, gender, and sexual orientation, MNO is open to everyone. We are committed to providing social and academic support to our members and we seek to create a forum for discussion about culture and its importance to the nursing practice.
In order to accomplish this goal, we hold programming that includes but is not limited to, talks with professors, hosting potlucks, and discussing how our individual cultures and/or background may impact our life at Penn and Penn Nursing. Other programming also includes community service events, study sessions, and social events such as game nights and movie screenings.
mno.how_to_get_involved: Follow our social media pages, join our listserv, and attend our events!

penn-climate-ventures.name: Climate Ventures at Penn
penn-climate-ventures.description:
Our Mission:
Climate Ventures at Penn (PCV) is a student-run organization dedicated to driving social impact in the environmental world. PCV aims to create a professional pipeline through consulting, finance, tech, and law— but specifically for climate! We are composed of students ranging from all four years and graduate students. We do not require any prior experience! 
What We Do:
Provide opportunities for students to gain real-world consulting and policy experiences, working with companies from nuclear energy to investment firms.
Teach fundamental skills for climate innovators through educational workshops and speaking events featuring founders, investors, and industry professionals working in climate and sustainability.
Empower student entrepreneurs in climate through our prize pitch competitions.
Host professional development and networking opportunities, including New York treks and company-sponsored dinners.
Foster a tight-knit and inclusive community by hosting social events like backyard potlucks, socials, board game nights, and more!
penn-climate-ventures.how_to_get_involved:
Fall 2026 Applications will be released via email and on our Instagram!
Undergraduate and graduate students from any major or school are eligible to apply. Positions are available in all committees. Always keep an eye out on our Penn Clubs and Instagram (@pennclimateventures) page....

penn-curling.name: Curling @ Penn
penn-curling.description:
The Curling team at Penn is a student group that practices out of the Philadelphia Curling Club every Saturday. Those who are interested in playing more competitively can participate in a number of tournaments throughout the winter across the Northeast US. Participating in these tournaments helps us collect points to qualify for Nationals at the end of the season.
We play against dozens of other colleges from near and far, often making friends with the teams from other schools. If competition and road trips aren't your speed, players are always welcome to only participate in a relaxed practice environment as well.
Learn a niche winter sport you've probably only ever seen during the Winter Olympics!
penn-curling.how_to_get_involved: Sign up for our Listserv or reach out to us on any social media platform and we'll get back to you ASAP.

penn-table-tennis.name: Table Tennis at Penn
penn-table-tennis.description:
Table Tennis at Penn is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that holds open practices. No tryouts or time commitments are required to join the club, so drop by any practice to say hi and play some ping pong!
If you're interested in competition, we have a recreational team that plays friendly scrimmages and a competitive team that travels to play schools around the country. Whether you are a beginner, an accomplished tournament player, or just someone looking to have fun - we have a place for you in our club!
penn-table-tennis.how_to_get_involved:
To join the club, simply show up to any practice. If you're interested in our competitive teams or representing the school at intercollegiate tournaments, talk to a club officer for more information. Also, register in Fusion Clubs at this link: https://club.fusionfamily.com/login 
Practice times for Fall 2026:
Sunday: 4:00pm - 6:00 pm
Tuesday: 5:30pm - 7:30pm
Thursday: 5:30pm - 7:30pm
Practices will be held at Weightman Hall (Google Maps Link).
Feel free to contact us by asking a question or sending us an e-mail. Hope to see you at practice!
Follow this link and click "Join group" if you'd like to be added to our mailing list: https://linktr.ee/penntabletennis. Please use your Penn email to register for the mailing list.

penn-graduate-consulting-club.name: Graduate Consulting Club at Penn
penn-graduate-consulting-club.description: Graduate Consulting Club at Penn (PGCC) is the largest student-run consulting club for non-MBA graduate students (PhDs, MDs, JDs, master's, etc.) and postdocs at the University of Pennsylvania. The purpose of our group is to serve the members of the Penn graduate and post-doctoral community who share a common interest in learning about careers in management consulting. To this end, we host multiple events, including an annual case competition, panel discussions, seminars, workshops, and lively networking receptions. Members can participate in pro bono consulting projects for real-world clients in order to gain hands-on experience in management consulting. We also create opportunities for our members to understand the perspectives of both experienced and freshly minted consultants. It is our goal to provide our 500+ members with an in-depth exposure to the consulting industry, and with ample support in preparing for case-based interviews.
penn-graduate-consulting-club.how_to_get_involved:
To become a member, please join our newsletter here. 
We would include the news of consulting, our recruitment info, events, and workshops in our weekly newsletters.
If you have any other questions, just email us @ pgcc.comm@gmail.com.
Find us on Instagram (@upenn_pgcc) and LinkedIn (Penn Graduate Consulting Club)!

womens-club-ice-hockey.name: Women's Club Ice Hockey
womens-club-ice-hockey.description: Women's Club Ice Hockey. We are a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania that is compromised of undergraduates and graduate students and beginners. We practice and play home games at the Class of 1923 Arena. Our season runs from September to February with around 20 games a season and two practices per week.
womens-club-ice-hockey.how_to_get_involved: Reach out to us via email or instagram! All schools/years welcome.

penn-raas.name: Raas at Penn
penn-raas.description:
Garba Raas is an energetic Indian folk dance originating in Gujarat that has now evolved into a full-fledged competitive dance circuit in America. Formed in 2007, Raas at Penn is UPenn's very own garba/raas team composed of both undergraduate and graduate students and is an official SAC funded University of Pennsylvania club. 
In addition to performing in front of our hometown crowd at Penn, we have traveled across the country competing in several competitions and even qualifying to compete at the Raas-All Stars National Championship in Dallas, TX in 2010. 
Each year, we hope to spread the passion of this dance form with traditional music mixed with upbeat tunes, a wildly vibrant choreographed dance piece, and strong facial energy that reflects the pure joy and fun of dancing with your friends that become family on stage. We are open to all undergraduate and graduate students at Penn!
penn-raas.how_to_get_involved: Follow us on Instagram @pennraas for information about workshops and tryouts! We post all of our information there. Feel free to DM us on IG with any questions!

black-undergraduate-entrepreneurship-col.name: Black Undergraduate Entrepreneurship Collective
black-undergraduate-entrepreneurship-col.description: The Black Undergraduate Entrepreneurship Collective (BUEC) is a student-run organization at Penn dedicated to making entrepreneurship accessible to undergraduate students by providing the tools and resources needed to launch their own ventures through the Black Founders Incubator, a 10-week program designed to teach the fundamentals of building a startup and help students create a minimum viable product. BUEC aims to cultivate a supportive community of entrepreneurs, enhance the visibility of established founders, and facilitate connections with diverse venture capitalists and funding sources to drive professional growth and entrepreneurial success. While our focus is on empowering entrepreneurship, BUEC is open to all Penn undergraduate and graduate students, regardless of identity, to join, engage in programming, and support our mission to uplift entrepreneurship.
black-undergraduate-entrepreneurship-col.how_to_get_involved: Follow our instagram @buec.upenn, sign up for our listerv, attend our events and apply for our Black Founders Incubator at the beginning of each semester!

penn-beekeeping.name: Beekeeping Club
penn-beekeeping.description: A student-run group that seeks to foster an appreciation for the ecological importance of the honeybee among students and members of the community. We keep bees on campus and host bee-related events for all bee-lievers in honey, pollinators, honeybees, and environmental protection! We welcome anyone and everyone to join, no prior experience necessary!
penn-beekeeping.how_to_get_involved: JOIN LISTSERV: http://eepurl.com/drI-4z to stay updated about events, and email thebeekeepingclub@gmail.com to learn how to be more involved!

science-olympiad.name: Science Olympiad at the University of Pennsylvania
science-olympiad.description:
Science Olympiad at the University of Pennsylvania (SOUP) is a student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania that hosts a Science Olympiad invitational tournament and mentors local middle school and high school teams in Philadelphia to spur interest in STEM for students who might otherwise lack the opportunity.
Our Purpose
Science Olympiad is a non-profit organization that hosts tournaments on a regional, state, and national level with around 7,800 teams of 15 students. These tournaments consist of 23 events that test students on a range of subjects, including biology, earth and space science, chemistry, and engineering. 
Our mission is to host the largest Science Olympiad invitational in the nation, providing young students nationwide the opportunity to experience Science Olympiad. We also run Urban Initiative to provide science mentorship and resources to students from underfunded high schools in Philadelphia.
science-olympiad.how_to_get_involved:
Our invitational will be on February 13th, 2027. Fill out this form if you are interested in joining SOUP.
You can also email us at any time at pennscienceolympiad@gmail.com to be added to our email list and Slack. Thank you!

americanredcross.name: Red Cross Club at Penn
americanredcross.description:
Red Cross Club at Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania which acts as a link between the Philadelphia Red Cross* chapter and Penn's campus.
We host volunteer opportunities like cooking dinners for Penn Transplant House patients, supporting our monthly blood drives, working to connect local families with appropriate services after disasters, and more! We also offer relevant, clinical opportunities for pre-health students like shadowing opportunities, speaker panels, and CPR classes. 
*The American Red Cross (ARC) is a humanitarian organization that provides emergency assistance, disaster relief and education inside the United States.
americanredcross.how_to_get_involved:
Email upenn.redcross@gmail.com
Follow our instagram for blood drive dates and join our Listserv for emails!

penn-tabletop.name: Tabletop at Penn
penn-tabletop.description: Tabletop at Penn brings students together through tabletop role-playing games (TTRPGs), including Dungeons & Dragons, homebrew campaigns, and Adventurers League adventures. We also foster a creative community for aspiring and experienced RPG developers, artists, and writers to develop, share, and playtest original science fiction and fantasy worlds, stories, and game content.
penn-tabletop.how_to_get_involved:
