It is open membership, so anyone can be a member with any level of commitment. We encourage members to attend all weekly meetings as able.
We have meetings on Saturdays in the Arch building! Join our Discord (dsc.gg/penn-tabletop) to see when our events are!

penn-undergraduate-charcuterie-club.name: Cheese Club at Penn
penn-undergraduate-charcuterie-club.description:
Cheese Club at Penn is a community for cheese lovers, whether you’re a seasoned connoisseur or simply curious about dairy’s finest creation. Our mission is to celebrate the art of cheese in all its forms through shared tasting, learning, and fun. 
Members can expect: 
Tasting Sessions – Sample everything from triple-cream brie to aged cheddar and adventurous blue cheeses. 
Workshops – Learn how cheese is made, find pairings and charcuterie, and even try your hand at cheesemaking. 
Cultural Exploration – Travel the world through cheese, from French classics to Spanish manchego to American farmstead wheels. 
Social Events – Gather for cheese boards, fondue nights, and potlucks. 
Educational Talks – Hear from local cheesemongers and food experts. 
Whether you’re here to refine your palate or just love a good cheese pull, our club celebrates the joy of cheese in all its glorious forms.

ues.name: Undergraduate Economics Society (UES)
ues.description: The Penn Undergraduate Economics Society (Penn UES) is the largest economics organization on campus, hosting events such as speaker series, professor chats, academic discussions, and more. We provide opportunities for academic and professional growth in all areas related to economics while fostering a strong community of students from diverse majors. All are welcome!
ues.how_to_get_involved:
To become a general body member, join our listserv here: UES Listserv. Committee applications are released via the listserv at the start of each semester, so make sure you’re subscribed. 
Fall 26 Interest Form: https://forms.gle/maih2XnjG5Rz1oRr7 (also joins Listserv)
Fall 26 Application: https://forms.gle/Z3jipi2RzR4b8Sv69 (also joins GBM)
UES Committees
ACADEMIC: Hosts discussions and writes articles on topics from healthcare to econometrics.
ALMANAC: Publishes the Economic Almanac, Penn’s first accessible economics publication, twice a year.
EVENTS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT: Runs events, workshops, and recruiting sessions for careers in research, academia, policy, management, finance, and consulting.
FINANCE & OUTREACH: Manages our budget and partnerships with sponsors, speakers, and alumni.
MARKETING: Promotes events, manages our social media, and designs our website and merchandise.

alpha-kappa-psi.name: Alpha Kappa Psi
alpha-kappa-psi.description:
As America's largest and oldest business fraternity, Alpha Kappa Psi has long prided itself as the premier developer of principled business leaders. For over 100 years, Alpha Kappa Psi has cultivated the world's leaders and innovators, seen from some of our alumni which include former Presidents Richard Nixon and Ronald Reagan, Wal-Mart Founder Sam Walton, publishing magnate Malcolm Forbes, and much more.
Here at Penn and Wharton, we are proud that our brothers continue to innovate not only within our fraternity but also with other organizations on campus and beyond. As just one example of AKPsi's leadership at the University of Pennsylvania, we recently established the Corporate Benefit, a ground-breaking event which connects our pillars of people, professionalism, and philanthropy. We hosted McDonald's CEO Jim Skinner, Johnson & Johnson's Vice Chairman Christine Poon, representatives from many of the most respected firms in the business world, and hundreds of Penn students for an evening to celebrate and support the Philadelphia community.
As brothers of Alpha Kappa Psi, we are united by our passion for business, commitment to brotherhood, and dedication to the community. Through the resources available exclusively to AKPsi brothers and the invaluable support we provide to one another, we count among our membership leaders of other campus organizations, members of Deans' Lists, successful entrepreneurs, and valued members of the community.
When our brothers move on after college, they join our worldwide alumni network -- stretching over 125,000 members -- more prepared, more confident, and more connected. Whether you are a prospective brother, treasured alumnus, collegiate colleague, or corporate partner, I invite you to see for yourself why we are all proud to call ourselves lifetime Brothers of Alpha Kappa Psi.
alpha-kappa-psi.how_to_get_involved: Rush occurs at the beginning of every semester. Check out our website or social media for more info!

theta-tau.name: Theta Tau
theta-tau.description:
Theta Tau is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania. As Penn's premier professional engineering fraternity, our purpose is to develop and maintain a high standard of professional interest among its members, and to unite them in a strong bond of fraternal fellowship.
Our three pillars of professional development, brotherhood, and service are reflected in our five-committee structure and complemented by our rush and pledge committees to keep membership fresh and enthusiastic. Please read on to learn more about the professional, social, and service-oriented aspects of our fraternity.
theta-tau.how_to_get_involved:
We hold rush every semester (in the spring for freshmen and sophomores, in the fall only for sophomores). Follow our Instagram page for more rush updates!
https://www.instagram.com/upenn.theta.tau

grandpas.name: Grandpas@Penn
grandpas.description: In this era of technology, social media has promoted toxic beauty standards among young people, causing college-age students to undergo anti-aging plastic surgery such as botox, facelifts, and liposuction. As a result of these unhealthy societal expectations, individuals forget that the process of aging is natural and beautiful. In an individualistic world that focuses almost entirely on the self, many people forget to appreciate the natural process of life. The mission of Grandpas@Penn is to challenge and de-stigmatize perceptions of aging within the Penn student body. Through exposure to narratives, experiences, and perspectives associated with later stages of life, we aim to help students reflect on aging as a process that can be deeply human. We host events for Penn students to connect with one another and realize that growing old is not something to fear, but a natural stage of life with many positive aspects.
grandpas.how_to_get_involved:
EVERYONE is welcome. NO application, NO rejections, ALL INCLUSIVE YAYYY
Request membership on Penn Clubs, follow us on Instagram, and come to our events to become a Grandpa @ Penn!!

wupp.name: Wharton Undergraduates in Public Policy
wupp.description:
WUPP is dedicated to promoting an interdisciplinary exploration of policy at Wharton and Penn that can be applied to all fields, from consulting to engineering, nonprofit work, and more. WUPP prepares students to become the next generation of leaders and change-makers in all that they do. We provide opportunities to consult for major policy organizations, conduct independent research and write original publications/articles, attend distinguished speaker events, and network with alumni and other professionals.
Our robust alumni network helps members stay connected with prestigious organizations in consulting, finance, technology, and government and discover their interests.
As a Wharton Council-recognized student organization, WUPP adheres to the University of Pennsylvania Policy on Equal Opportunity. All Penn undergraduates are welcome to sign up to participate in WUPP's general body membership (GBM) events and programs.
wupp.how_to_get_involved: Applications will re-open in the Fall 2026 Semester. See you then!

women-in-physics.name: Women in Physics
women-in-physics.description: Women in Physics (WiP) at the University of Pennsylvania aims to support undergraduate students of marginalized genders who are underrepresented in physics. We strive to create an inclusive community by hosting casual study breaks and peer mentorship opportunities, alongside professional development opportunities and speaker events. WiP invites students of all gender identities who support the advancement of women in physics to join.
women-in-physics.how_to_get_involved: Fill out our interest form here to join our mailing list! We welcome people from all class years, genders and majors!

penn-appetit.name: The Appétit
penn-appetit.description: The Appétit is the University of Pennsylvania's innovative, student-run magazine covering all things food. Throughout the year, we publish eye-catching magazines, host events with high-profile restaurateurs, and trek through Philly and beyond for the greatest food finds. Find a place in our organization by becoming a writer, photographer, designer, or recipe developer! If you want more hands-on experiences, you can help us plan a new host of events, establish relations within the food industry, run our food blog, or volunteer directly in the Philly community, to name a few.
penn-appetit.how_to_get_involved: Check our website and Instagram (@pennappetit) in early September and late January. We'll post lots of information on how to join there when the time comes!

aipenn.name: AI@Penn
aipenn.description:
AI@Penn is the premier AI student organization at Penn, backed by the Raj and Neera Singh AI Program and the Wharton AI & Analytics Initiative. Dedicated to developing industry-level applications, research and incubating startups in Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Computer Vision etc. 
AI@Penn consists of four key branches and a GBM:
Development – Dedicated to creating impactful AI applications by utilizing established models, frameworks, and architectures to address real-world challenges.
Research – Focused on advancing AI through collaboration with Penn professors and industry experts. 
Outreach – Acts as a bridge between the Penn AI community and top industry leaders, including companies like HF, AWS, Meta, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Apple. 
Entrepreneurship - Serves as an incubator for students eager to transform their AI-related ideas into impactful real-world ventures, leveraging resources from the innovation ecosystem on campus and our industry partners. 
Our GBM Engagement will have a 100% acceptance rate.

snugs.name: SNUGS (Special Needs Undergraduate Swim Lessons)
snugs.description:
SNUGS is a non-profit, national organization, with a student group chapter of the organization at the University of Pennsylvania. Our core mission aims to decrease the number of drownings amongst children with special needs, which is the #1 cause of death for children with intellectual disabilities. By providing free swim instruction, with your help, we believe we can make a huge difference.
Many university campuses, such as UPenn, are situated near low income communities, where specialized swimming lessons are too expensive for financially-burdened parents with disabled children. Special Needs Undergraduate Swim Lessons (SNUGS) brings free, one-on-one, personalized water safety and technique clinics to these areas. SNUGS is also currently active at 7 universities nation-wide and is still expanding. 
Please help us fulfill our mission and provide free swim lessons to those in and around our community. No prior experience is necessary.
snugs.how_to_get_involved: Email us at penn@snugsnational.org letting us know that you're interested in volunteering and we'll respond with more information!

the-excelano-project.name: The Excelano Project
the-excelano-project.description:
The Excelano Project is the University of Pennsylvania’s first and premier spoken word group. Supposedly derived from Latin, “excelano” means “we march forth” and from its foundation in 2001 by poets and then Penn students Carlos Gomez and Warren Longmire, EP has been doing just that. In 2007 and 2009, we had the pleasure of taking home the College Union’s Poetry Slam Invitational title. Our poets have been featured at the White House, on HBO, at the famous Nuyorican Poets Cafe, on Broadway, and all around the world.
But EP goes beyond the poetry; we are a family. This group is about finding voice. It is dedicated to the power of the mic and using personal experience to touch the lives of audience members. It’s about breaking down barriers. It’s about holding a speaker up to life’s white noise, to find that every one of us can be heard.
the-excelano-project.how_to_get_involved: Please see our Instagram @excelanoproject for our updated auditions information and dates!

penn-atma.name: Atma
penn-atma.description: Atma is Penn's award-winning, female-identifying South Asian fusion a cappella student group! Since the inception of the group at the University of Pennsylvania in 2002, Atma has been most noted for bringing together a wide variety of genres to create a deep and unique sound. Today, the ladies of Atma continue to develop musically, exploring new sounds and ideas, and driving performances with expression and personality.
penn-atma.how_to_get_involved:
Auditions occur in the first 2 weeks of each semester.
Stay tuned for audition updates on our Instagram! @penn_atma

wharton-undergraduate-finance-club.name: Wharton Undergraduate Finance Club
wharton-undergraduate-finance-club.description:
The Wharton Undergraduate Finance Club (WUFC) is a student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to being a comprehensive destination for all students interested in finance. We believe a strong foundation in financial knowledge and industry exposure should be accessible to every student, and our mission centers on closing that gap.
From education to recruiting to networking, WUFC supports students at every stage of their journey into finance. As Wharton's most prominent and largest finance-focused organization, we are committed to promoting equal access to the industry and empowering every member to achieve their professional goals.
wharton-undergraduate-finance-club.how_to_get_involved:
WUFC is comprised of Educational Committees (Investment Team, Quant Finance Team, Case Team, Capital Advisory) and Internal Committees (Corporate Relations, Marketing, Events). Applications for committees are required through the centralized Penn Clubs website.
Our GBM program meets weekly on Tuesdays and does not require an application. To be a part of our GBM program, please join our email chain linked on our website.
To get access to our weekly newsletters and upcoming events, join our listserv via our website https://www.whartonundergradfinance.com/
All Links: https://linktr.ee/whartonundergradfinance

netter-center-student-advisory-board.name: Netter Center Student Advisory Board
netter-center-student-advisory-board.description:
The Netter Center brings together the resources and assets of both the University and the wider community to help solve universal problems such as poverty, health inequities, environmental sustainability, and inadequate, and unequal education. The Netter Center Student Advisory Board was formed in 2001 to increase student involvement in the operation and strategic planning of the Netter Center. 
Members work to deepen and improve the engagement of students involved in the Netter Center, as well as to inform and engage the wider Penn community. This includes increasing the visibility of the Center and its programs; establishing connections between the Center and key contacts in the Penn community (e.g. student groups, academic departments); and providing strategic advice and counsel to the Center's many programs.
netter-center-student-advisory-board.how_to_get_involved:
SAB members are students who have been involved in Netter Center programming or ABCS courses and are usually selected by Netter staff members. 
Beyond joining the student advisory board, you can visit Netter's website to get involved in ABCS courses or service programs!

onda-latina.name: Onda Latina
onda-latina.description:
In the Fall of 1996, a small group of students had the vision to educate the Penn community about Caribbean and Latino culture through dance. Together they founded Onda Latina, which means "Latin Wave," Penn's first and only dance group of its kind. 
Onda Latina has become an immensely popular name on this campus and in the Philadelphia community performing to sold-out crowds every semester. Over the years, the Onda Latina family has grown to over 45 members, bringing together many ethnic backgrounds, unique talents, and fresh ideas. Our passion for dance, however, goes far beyond Penn's campus. We accept auditionees from all Phildelphia area universities, we guest perform for various campus organizations and events, and we also spread our special flavor throughout the community and at other colleges and universities. Our goal is to continue our tradition as promoters of education, entertainment, and the true experience of dance: fun.
onda-latina.how_to_get_involved: Follow us on social media, come to our events, and chat with our members!

intuitions.name: iNtuitons Experimental Theatre
intuitions.description:
iNtuitons Experimental Theatre is the University of Pennsylvania's only student-run experimental theatre group. iNtuitons comes from two words: intuition and automaton. The group was chartered to "attract people with diverse artistic interests and in order to provide an outlet for creative people whose ideas are too Classical or Avant-Garde to be supported by existing groups."
Each year we present a student-directed mainstage production in the fall and spring, our annual Alternative Theatre Festival featuring student submissions (part of Philly FringeArts Festival), plus participating in the Theatre Arts Council's One Acts Festival each winter. We've also had bonus shows (winter & spring), play-readings of original work by Philadelphia artists, and guerilla theatre experiments.
Our "taste" is broad in scope. iNtuitons has produced work by such diverse writers as Vaclav Havel, Sarah Kane, Euripides, Joseph Conrad, Sam Shepard, Milan Kundera, Caryl Churchill... just to name a few.
intuitions.how_to_get_involved:
Production staff or cast for a show: Audition for a performing role in the cast or interview for a technical role on the prod staff! We hold auditions/interviews three times a year (Fall, Winter, Spring) with the rest of the TAC-e groups. Reach out to any board member about how to get involved and stay updated on our socials!
Board member: We hold board elections every spring (~March)! Attend board meetings, pick the shows we put up for our upcoming seasons, get involved as a producer, and help make theatre experimental!

international-fgli-ifgli.name: international FGLI (iFGLI)
international-fgli-ifgli.description: iFGLI is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania focused on supporting international limited income and/or first generation students (iFGLIs). Our main goal is to provide support and community and to advocate for every single iFGLI, recognizing the diversity of experiences and realities of our global campus community. We are open to all students.

penn-venture-group.name: Wharton Undergraduate Venture Group
penn-venture-group.description:
Wharton Undergraduate Venture Group is a student organization at Penn giving driven students hands-on experience evaluating and pitching startup investments to top VC firms and consulting innovative startups. 
We’re dedicated to providing VC firms with insights on industry trends and emerging companies and we strive to assist early-stage ventures in crafting and executing their growth strategy.
penn-venture-group.how_to_get_involved: Thank you for your interest in WUVG! Our group consists of three arms: Venture Capital Research, Startup Consulting, and Corporate Outreach. Please click this link to be added to our listserv, and follow our instagram @whartonventuregroup to keep up with info sessions and application deadlines.

upgrade.name: UPGRADE
upgrade.description:
UPGRADE is Penn's premier game development group. Every year, we produce two club-wide games, one every semester. The second semester game is published on Steam with your name in the credits! Anyone can join our club, and we do not require applications.
We provide the resources, opportunities, and environment to foster passion and creativity. We host yearly game jams, organize training workshops, present speaker talks, travel to fun events (such as GDC and PAX EAST), and more!
Whether you like programming, drawing, modeling, writing, composing, or anything, we welcome anyone interested in any aspect of games. While previous experience with any of these roles is expected, you'll hit the ground running and you'll make your very first game in a matter of days!
upgrade.how_to_get_involved:
Prospective members must join our Discord (our main form of communication): https://discord.gg/wPyhsyuTQ6
Meeting times: Saturdays 2pm - 5pm in Towne 217 ALC. Office Hours: Wednesdays 8pm in Levine 057 
Attend our weekly meetings and check in with us during OH/grind sessions whenever necessary. Join our Discord: https://discord.gg/wPyhsyuTQ6. Other than that, try to work on your games throughout the week instead of leaving it until the end!

page.name: Penn Association for Gender Equity (PAGE)
page.description: The Penn Association for Gender Equity (PAGE) promotes gender and social justice and serves as an umbrella organization for a diverse range of constituent groups at Penn that serve people of martinalized genders.
page.how_to_get_involved:
PAGE focuses on three pillars: advocacy, community-building, and education. Interested in getting involved with gender equity on campus and/or attending programming related to gender equity? Subscribe to our newsletter and follow us on Instagram @penngenderequity! 
For anyone interested in publicity for their event/program who would like to have something published in our newsletter, please email us at contact.pagechair@gmail.com.
This fall, PAGE will be hosting First-Year Fellows (FYF). With support from facilitators, first years and transfer students will be able to discuss their feminist experiences and analyze the meaning of inclusivity on small and large scales. The goal of FF is to not only educate but to also create a healing community among the fellows, their facilitators, and PAGE. Follow us on Facebook and Instagram to get updates! The link to the application can be found on our Instagram.
Elections for PAGE board will happen in December. Anyone is welcome to run for a position! We also host events and GBMs that are open to all Penn students interested in gender equity. This semester, GBMs are hosted at the Penn Women's Center on the following dates at 8PM: October 28 and December 1.
If you are interested in getting involved with PAGE, fill out our interest form here (https://forms.gle/UJVRNoe5Ki9kqkRb6).

upenn-alt-protein-project.name: The Alt Protein Project at Penn
upenn-alt-protein-project.description: The Alt Protein Project at Penn is a chapter of the Good Food Institute (GFI) Alt Protein Project, a global student movement dedicated to turning universities into engines for alternative protein education, research, and innovation. The program enables motivated, visionary students to lead their universities to transform the way we produce food - creating a food system that is sustainable, secure, and just. The Alt Protein Project is focused on generating awareness and excitement, stimulating open-access research, catalyzing entrepreneurship, building alternative protein courses and majors, and creating an inclusive and inspiring community!
upenn-alt-protein-project.how_to_get_involved:
If you are interested or want to learn more about the Alt Protein Project at Penn, please reach out directly to alexzaz@sas.upenn.edu or mayami@sas.upenn.edu! Application details can be found on our Instagram.
Fall 2026 applications open August 25th and close September 3rd!

penn-international-impact-consulting.name: Penn International Impact Consulting (PIIC)
penn-international-impact-consulting.description:
A Bit About PIIC
PIIC (pronounced “peak”) is a student-run group at Penn, providing pro-bono consulting services to NGOs and social entrepreneurs worldwide.
We’re committed to empowering social entrepreneurs in developing regions through meaningful work and international on-site visits. We've worked across impact areas including healthcare, education, water sanitation, conservation, and refugee rights.
Our consultants work in teams with a partner NGO on deliverables throughout the school year, then travel to the NGO’s headquarters in May. This allows us to build deep engagements with our partners and their communities. Our overall goal is to take what we’ve learned at Penn and during our unique training sessions to create sustainable and long-term social impact for our partners.
Since our founding, we’ve made good on our mission to create long-lasting global change. We have visited more than 45 countries, partnering with more than 90 unique NGOs.
penn-international-impact-consulting.how_to_get_involved: We will be recruiting an incoming cohort of Associate Consultants this fall. Class of '29 and Class of '30 from all schools and majors are welcome to apply! Be sure to follow our Instagram Page (piic.upenn) and visit https://penniic.org/fall-recruiting for all the info on the 2026 Recruiting Cycle including our events, videos, projects, interview tips, and much more. Also, be sure to hit the bookmark and bell on the top right of this page to stay up to date with our upcoming events and recruiting cycle. Learn about how you can make an impact, build professional skills, discover career opportunities, and become a part of our PIIC family 🌏

distressed-investing-group.name: Wharton Undergraduate Distressed Investing Group (WUDIG)
distressed-investing-group.description:
Wharton Undergraduate Distressed Investing Group (WUDIG) is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania that serves as a resource for undergraduate students interested in distressed investing and restructuring. 
WUDIG seeks to provide educational content and a forum for discussion within Penn for undergraduates interested in pursuing careers as restructuring consultants, financial advisors to distressed companies and their creditors, or investors in distressed securities across the capital structure. 
WUDIG also provides students with a professional network for development within the distressed investing space and leverages the expertise of industry professionals, especially Wharton alumni.
distressed-investing-group.how_to_get_involved: We are recruiting members for Fall 2026. Reach out to whartonrx@gmail.com if you have any questions.

mens-club-ultimate-frisbee.name: Men's Club Ultimate Frisbee
mens-club-ultimate-frisbee.description:
Men's Club Ultimate Frisbee (Void) is a student group open to all students at the University of Pennsylvania. Void was founded in 1976 and is the longest continuously-run Ultimate program in Philadelphia. We compete as a D1 Men’s College Ultimate program. Our program has won one national championship (1985) and has alumni playing at the highest levels of club and professionally in the AUDL.
We offer an A team and a B team, called Null. While Void is competitive in nature, we do not cut from the program. Anyone who wants to play on Null can. Our goals as a club are to introduce the sport and grow love for Ultimate on Null, and to compete at the highest levels on Void.
Although we have tryouts for Void, we don't cut from the program. Any person who would like to play club ultimate at Penn has that opportunity.
mens-club-ultimate-frisbee.how_to_get_involved: Fill out this form to be put on our email list for updates and inclusion in events this fall: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeu17F_E0hL5UTgy5N-rEl0LC7Y9Juf8pOHjC0dtnb05NPuug/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=108698698780806635243

pennyo-a-cappella.name: PennYo A Cappella
pennyo-a-cappella.description:
PennYo is Penn's premier Chinese student a cappella group and the first collegiate Chinese a cappella group in the United States. We hope to spread the love for Chinese music to the Philadelphia community and beyond. We welcome students of all backgrounds to audition! Chinese proficiency is not required (we have members from all around the world)!
All of our arrangements are written by current and past PennYo members. Check out our instagram
pennyo-a-cappella.how_to_get_involved:
We will be holding auditions next year in Fall 2027. 
Don't forget to check out our Instagram (@pennyoacappella) or website (https://www.pennyo.us) for show information and updates.

jewish-heritage-programs.name: Jewish Heritage Programs
jewish-heritage-programs.description: Jewish Heritage Programs (JHP) is a student-run organization through Chabad at Penn built upon four pillars: social action, community service, mentoring, and Jewish content. Using peer-to-peer programming to engage and energize individuals not typically involved in Jewish communal activities, JHP empowers each individual to understand their own ability to have an impact in making the world a better place.

soundworks.name: Soundworks Tap Factory
soundworks.description: We are a completely student-choreographed group that performs in and produces two shows each academic year. Our unique style comes from the broad dance foundation of all our members, which includes rhythm tap, Broadway-style tap, hip-hop, jazz, and more!
soundworks.how_to_get_involved: Spring 2027 audition times will be released shortly!

matriculate.name: Matriculate
matriculate.description:
Welcome to Penn Matriculate! We are a student organization at Penn and a community of college students that virtually advise high-achieving, low-income high school students, and help them apply to colleges across the country. 
Upon acceptance, each member will be paired with up to four high school students to mentor. In addition to advising high schoolers, we hold monthly and community events and offer opportunities for leadership to members of all class years and backgrounds.
Matriculate is a national nonprofit and has chapters at 16 institutions including Columbia, Princeton, Yale, Stanford, Johns Hopkins, Notre Dame, UCLA, & Berkeley.
Also, follow us on IG for the most up-to-date information!

penn-quiz-bowl.name: Quizbowl Club at Penn
penn-quiz-bowl.description: A student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to competing in intercollegiate quiz bowl tournaments. Our mission is to foster academic curiosity, teamwork, and a welcoming community while representing the University of Pennsylvania at the regional and national levels.
penn-quiz-bowl.how_to_get_involved:
Join our email list at https://forms.gle/XJ2TbPU6hvTHmHeo9 to stay up-to-date with our goings-on! Or email us at pennquizbowl@gmail.com if you have any questions!
Our club holds weekly practices where members can sharpen their knowledge, improve buzzer speed, and enjoy friendly scrimmages. Throughout the year, we travel to compete against other colleges and universities, representing Penn at the regional and national level.
FALL 26 MEETING TIMES (each week): 
Monday 8-10 PM, JMHH F36
Thursday 8-10 PM, JMHH F36

judo.name: Judo Club
judo.description:
Judo is a grappling martial art that includes throws, pins, chokes, and armbars. We compete at local competitions, as well as the annual PCJA college tournament. We welcome all skill levels, so come try out a session with us! 
Judo Club is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania, and is affiliated with the Philadelphia Collegiate Judo Association, which is an umbrella organization that includes college clubs at Swarthmore, St. Joseph's, Bryn Mawr, Haverford, and West Chester University.
judo.how_to_get_involved: Join the Facebook group for timely updates, as that is where we most regularly update our members!

penn-minhuet.name: MINHUET at the University of Pennsylvania
penn-minhuet.description:
MINHUET is a community service student group at the University of Pennsylvania that brings live performances from Penn’s music and arts community into West Philadelphia’s nursing homes and hospitals. Our objective is to construct meaningful and positive relationships between Penn students and the elderly or ill through the power of music.
Patients in nursing homes and hospitals have to stave off loneliness, displacement, and isolation, all while enduring substantial distress. Current research demonstrates that live music meets some of their many needs by providing not only sources of diversion and entertainment but also feelings of texture, time, and place — forms of self-awareness that are beneficial therapeutically.
MINHUET volunteers are given complete freedom in their performances, which in turn will be coordinated with any requests of the healthcare facilities we serve; Volunteers can choose to perform solo repertoire or form a chamber group upon request.
penn-minhuet.how_to_get_involved:
We are currently looking for musicians for 2026-2027. If interested, join the Slack or mailing list to learn more!
Link to mailing list: http://eepurl.com/jmQLfk

penn-reproductive-justice-working-group.name: Reproductive Justice Working Group at Penn
penn-reproductive-justice-working-group.description:
Reproductive Justice Working Group is a community-centered student group at Penn striving to protect reproductive and sexual justice by fighting for increased contraceptive & abortion access, comprehensive sex ed, repro health legislation, menstrual equity, and much more. We support repro justice work in both the Penn & Philly community by amplifying local advocacy efforts, distributing educational resources and contraceptives/menstrual products, and developing sustainable and meaningful connections with our partner orgs.
PRJ aims to create a positive culture of enthusiasm, proactiveness, and initiative. As a member, you will be empowered to become a community-conscious advocate for reproductive justice. Anyone can be an activist, and we want to give you the tools to create change! We also want to foster connection in the repro justice space, so look out for check-in’s with our lead organizers and social events where you can build community with other activists!
penn-reproductive-justice-working-group.how_to_get_involved:
We are a very welcoming and supportive group of people who are excited to get to know you! Anyone can join our listserv through this Google Form (https://forms.gle/bw2EYzmwGRK6wyts6), where we will have weekly newsletters to update you on our meetings, events, and initiatives. 
We will send out committee applications at the start of each semester in our newsletter and Instagram.
Feel free to email upennreproductivejustice@gmail.com with any questions!

spec-to-represent-undergraduate-minoriti.name: SPEC To Represent Undergraduate Minorities (SPEC-TRUM)
spec-to-represent-undergraduate-minoriti.description:
Welcome to the SPEC-TRUM Committee, a branch of the Social Planning and Events Committee (SPEC) and a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. 
SPEC-TRUM (To Represent Undergraduate Minorities) events vary from free skates and movie nights to concerts, to our Tiny Desk Showcase, and in the past they have included concerts with Tierra Whack, SiR, Rico Nasty, DRAM, Aminé, and the Roots. SPEC-TRUM is open to all Penn students.
For more information on everything TRUM see our powerpoint!
spec-to-represent-undergraduate-minoriti.how_to_get_involved: Feel free to fill out this short form at http://eepurl.com/76pYf to be added to our listserv! Easiest way to get involved is to attend our General Body Meetings (GBMs) and by following our social media pages to get updates as to what we've been doing!

spec-sound.name: SPEC Sound
spec-sound.description: We provide, maintain, and run the technical equipment for events hosted by a variety of student organizations, including sororities and fraternities, cultural events, bands, and more. Plus, we pay our members who work these events!
spec-sound.how_to_get_involved: No applications are required to join any of SPEC's committees. No experience necessary - we will have training sessions during the beginning of each semester and throughout the semester when needed for new members!

association-of-black-women-in-dentistry.name: Association of Black Aspiring Dentists
association-of-black-women-in-dentistry.description:
The Association of Black Aspiring Dentists (ABAD) is the first and only student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania focused on highlighting and advancing the experiences of Black pre-dental students. While our mission emphasizes uplifting Black voices in dentistry, membership is open to all students who share an interest in promoting diversity, accessibility, and equity in the profession.
ABAD fosters success through impactful mentorship with dental students, community events in collaboration with local schools, and discussions led by accomplished dental professionals. These conversations span a diverse range of topics, including oral surgery, periodontal care, advancements in dental technology, and overall well-being.
association-of-black-women-in-dentistry.how_to_get_involved:
We’re on a mission to make our Philadelphia-based club an engaging hub for students interested in dentistry and the experiences of Black aspiring dentists! Whether you’re passionate about pursuing dentistry or simply curious to learn more, there are plenty of ways to dive in. Join us for our orientation to discover our goals and activities, and connect with fellow students through collaborations with other local clubs.
Mark your calendar for interactive events, where you’ll gain hands-on experience through workshops and learn from inspiring guest speakers. Don’t miss out on membership perks, and share your journey on social media to encourage others to join the conversation.
We’re all about building a supportive and inclusive community. Members can help shape the future of ABAD by mentoring peers, sharing feedback through surveys, and participating in regular community service opportunities that allow us to make a collective impact. Your involvement is what makes our association thrive, and we can’t wait to see the energy you’ll bring!
Link to our GBM Form for the 25/26 Academic Year: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfqZOvVEBCaBi9c_PI1W2GTzK8luOAL86R0LqmM3nDX83hizA/viewform

pennlabs.name: Penn Labs
pennlabs.description: We are a team of student software engineers, product designers, and business developers. Our ultimate goal is improving the Penn community with technology. In addition to creating 100% free high-quality products, we give back with educational resources and technical support.
pennlabs.how_to_get_involved:
We recruit new members at the beginning of each semester. Join our listserv to learn more when applications are released, as well as incoming info sessions.
Apply at https://pennclubs.com/club/pennlabs/apply

rapline.name: Reach-A-Peer Helpline
rapline.description:
RAP-Line is a peer helpline established by Penn students to provide peer support, information, and referrals. It's open to all students who wish to share a problem, are in need of information, or just want to talk to someone anonymously and confidentially. The service is run by trained student volunteers who have an awareness of campus resources and skills in active listening techniques. Volunteers acknowledge that they're not professional counselors, but rather peers who provide a warm, unbiased, and supportive environment conducive to self-help. RAP-Line is a stepping-stone in serving the Penn community. The phone call is free, anonymous, and confidential. 
RAP-Line offers two services:
1. 24/7 Text Line
Send a message to 215-515-7332 to connect anonymously with a RAP-Line peer supporter.
2. Phone Line
The Line is available every night from 9 pm to 1 am. Reach us at 215-573-2727. Don't be shy!
rapline.how_to_get_involved:
We are recruiting members for our Fall 2026 Training Class! The application link is below.
https://forms.gle/gtQDNmo9j2Rnxemu7
Please direct any questions to training.rapline@gmail.com.

penn-to-paper.name: Pen to Paper
penn-to-paper.description:
Pen to Paper is a student organization dedicated to creative writing. Through workshops, critique circles, mentorship, and other activities, we hope to cultivate and uplift the creative voices of students coming from marginalized backgrounds. Often, people with these identities feel pressured to speak solely about one experience or not speak at all. We want Pen to Paper to be an avenue through which everyone can write freely. Whether you’ve had a fascinating idea swimming around your mind for ages but don’t know where to start or you’d like some advice on how to best move your story along, we’re here to help you finally put pen to paper!
Members are not required to have any prior creative writing experience. Anyone interested in joining needs only to come with their imagination and a pen!
penn-to-paper.how_to_get_involved:
Please fill out this form if you're interested in joining us!
Membership Form: https://forms.gle/jghucDkB5CusBpbx7

the-penn-epistle.name: The Epistle at Penn
the-penn-epistle.description:
The Epistle at Penn is a Christian journal dedicated to sharing and echoing the words of Christ's followers. We encourage and accept all students from diverse backgrounds to share their testimonies, emotions, beliefs, and experiences about their religious journeys. This organization hopes to become a vessel for the Lord's words in order to comfort, support, and inspire believers and nonbelievers to pursue and deepen their faith.
We publish in print twice annually, once in the winter with our zine, The In-Between, and once in the fall with our full-length magazine! Otherwise, we post multiple articles a month on our blog and create video and podcast content.
Anyone and everyone is welcome to join this community and write for the Epistle at Penn!
the-penn-epistle.how_to_get_involved: Please complete this interest form, and we will get back to you shortly!

the-accountability-initiative.name: The Accountability Initiative
the-accountability-initiative.description: The Accountability Initiative-Penn chapter is a student led organization of young advocates at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to connecting the UPenn and West Philadelphia Community through advocacy, mentorship, and service. We offer Higher Education workshops to West Philadelphia High Schools on topics ranging from College Readiness and Financial Literacy to Trade School and Resume Building.
the-accountability-initiative.how_to_get_involved: Interested people can get involved by visiting our Instagram account, where they can find information on signing up for West Philly High School workshops or getting involved with our on-campus events. Community service opportunities will as also be advertised around campus.

uss.name: Wharton Undergraduate Statistics Society (USS)
uss.description:
The Wharton Undergraduate Statistics Society (USS) is your resource for all things statistics at Penn. The Wharton Undergraduate Statistics Society is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. Each year, the USS puts on a plethora of fun and engaging events, broadly under three categories:
Events: Professional development opportunities like research panels, professor talks, and coding workshops; social events like pizza mixers, study breaks, and course advice!
Academic Journal: Sharing statistical research on our website and writing articles each semester. 
Tutoring: Volunteer tutoring opportunities for middle school students in the West Philadelphia community.
The USS operates in a three-tier structure:
Executive board
Committee members
General body members
uss.how_to_get_involved: Sign up to be on our listserv to be a general body member! If you would like a more direct role within USS, please fill out the application on PennClubs to apply to be a Deputy VP for a committee. Deputy VPs will be picked beginning of every semester!

penn-astronomical-student-association.name: Astronomy at Penn
penn-astronomical-student-association.description: Astronomy at Penn (also known as AAP) aspires to foster a community of students as a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania, welcoming all majors and backgrounds who are interested in astronomy, science fiction, and everything in between.
penn-astronomical-student-association.how_to_get_involved:
In line with our mission to be a relaxed, accepting environment, no applications are required. Simply come to any of our events and bring some friends, too! If you're interested in obtaining a board position to help us run events and spread the word about AAP to the Penn community, please email us for more information and follow us on our instagram: @pennastro
Fill out this form to sign up for our listserv: https://forms.gle/5Wg1sJPDHbe44SUk7 or join our discord here.

medical-volunteers-for-prevention.name: Medical Volunteers for Prevention
medical-volunteers-for-prevention.description: The US healthcare system is one that is overextended and inequitable and, as a result, preventative care, a crucial aspect of healthcare, is often overlooked. Teaching and encouraging a preventative lifestyle is a form of healthcare that can, and will, make a difference in the health of many communities. Medical Volunteers for Prevention is a student-run group at the University of Pennsylvania that aims to reach various communities and provide them with the knowledge to lead a healthy lifestyle. Whether it be older communities where Osteoporosis is prevalent or marginalized communities through which navigating healthcare insurance seems impossible, our goal is to provide individuals with healthcare knowledge so that they can take back their health, minimize their risk of injury and disease, and advocate for their needs in a medical setting.
medical-volunteers-for-prevention.how_to_get_involved:
The application for FA26 is open! Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
https://forms.gle/H2CxAR9ktadaHPco8 
Feel free to email if you have questions.

queer-and-asian.name: Queer and Asian
queer-and-asian.description:
Queer and Asian (Q&A) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to providing a safe space for the support and empowerment of LGBTQ+ and allied individuals interested in addressing issues of the queer Asian community.
We host numerous social and discussion events each semester. Past events have included boba socials, chai chats, Valentine's Day mixer, ConversAsians (discussions on being Q&A), game/movie nights, picnics, and lots of other fun activities!
queer-and-asian.how_to_get_involved:
You don't have to request membership here! Please fill out this form to join our listserv and receive weekly newsletters: https://forms.gle/t6CC6qHCWPsvXnGm8 
Follow us on Instagram (@pennqanda) and feel free to email us (pennqanda@gmail.com) with any questions!

penn-kendo-and-iaido-club.name: Kendo Club at Penn
penn-kendo-and-iaido-club.description:
The Kendo Club at Penn is a student organization dedicated to the practice of kendo, the Japanese martial art of swordsmanship.
We are a beginner-friendly club that fosters a welcoming and supportive environment where students of all skill levels can develop physical skill, mental discipline, and spiritual growth through training.
Recognized by the All United States Kendo Federation (AUSKF) and affiliated with Cherry Hill Kenyu Kai under the Eastern United States Kendo Federation (EUSKF), we offer opportunities for both personal development and competitive participation in intercollegiate tournaments. 
Come practice with us!
penn-kendo-and-iaido-club.how_to_get_involved: Find us on Instagram @pennkendo or send us an email to get connected!

penn-electric-racing.name: Electric Racing at Penn
penn-electric-racing.description: Electric Racing at Penn is a student engineering organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to designing, building, testing, and validating competitive electric race cars. Electric Racing at Penn provides students with hands-on experience in mechanical, electrical, software, and operations work while developing technical, leadership, and project management skills. Through full-cycle vehicle development and annual Formula SAE Electric competition, Electric Racing at Penn aims to advance student engineering education, strengthen collaboration across disciplines, and represent Penn in collegiate electric vehicle innovation.
penn-electric-racing.how_to_get_involved: Please keep an eye out on our Penn Clubs page and our instagram @pennelectricracing for recruitment updates!

penn-undergraduate-founders-and-funders-.name: Wharton Undergraduate Founders and Funders Association
penn-undergraduate-founders-and-funders-.description: The Wharton Undergraduate Founders and Funders Association (WUFFA) is a student group at Penn that seeks to increase the number of women and underrepresented founders and investors in the start-up ecosystem. We are a group of technologists, aspiring founders and investors, engineers, and designers who are passionate about learning from each other and Penn Wharton alumni. We value diversity of background, thought and experience and we welcome anyone who is interested in entrepreneurship, investing, and consulting to apply.
penn-undergraduate-founders-and-funders-.how_to_get_involved: Applications for our investment and consulting committees are open! In addition to our committees, we have 2 speaker events per semester open to anyone who signs up for our listserv. Listserv members also receive access to startup and investing internship opportunities.

active-minds.name: Active Minds
active-minds.description: Active Minds was founded in 2001 by Alison Malmon at the University of Pennsylvania and has since then grown into a national nonprofit organization with college chapters across the country. We are a student-run mental health awareness, education, and advocacy organization on campus. Our mission is to increase students' awareness of mental health issues, provide information and resources regarding mental health, encourage students to seek help as soon as it is needed, and serve as liaison between students and the mental health community. Through campus-wide events and community service, Active Minds aims to eliminate the stigma surrounding mental health issues, and create a comfortable environment for an open conversation about mental health issues on campus.
active-minds.how_to_get_involved: Email activemindspenn@gmail.com with your name and class year to get involved! Also, Join Our Listserv!

the-penn-walk.name: Models@Penn
the-penn-walk.description:
Models@Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to empowering students to embrace their individuality and build confidence through runway modeling. 
We strive to create a diverse and inclusive community that nurtures creativity, collaboration, and personal growth while helping members refine their runway skills and stage presence. 
Our goal is to provide a platform for aspiring models to develop their craft, gain experience, and explore professional opportunities in the world of modeling, all while fostering a supportive and inspiring environment within the Penn community.
the-penn-walk.how_to_get_involved:
Complete our General Member Interest Form to join our community and receive Instagram updates about meetings, workshops, castings, photoshoots, fashion shows, and other opportunities. General Member Interest Form 
Follow us on Instagram for upcoming events and announcements. Instagram 
Interested in joining our leadership team? Fill out the Executive Board Application here. Executive Board Application

locust-line-swing-society.name: Locust Line & Swing Society
locust-line-swing-society.description:
Welcome to the Locust Line & Swing Society!🤠🤠🤠
The Locust Line & Swing Society is a vibrant and welcoming community of country dance enthusiasts at the University of Pennsylvania. Whether you're an experienced dancer or a complete beginner, our club offers an exciting and inclusive space to explore the rhythmic and joyful world of country line dancing, two-stepping, and country swing. Our dance nights are announced on our social pages and typically will occur monthly.
No matter your level of experience, if you have an interest in learning how to dance or simply vibing to country music, our club is the perfect place for you to express yourself, learn new skills, and enjoy the camaraderie of fellow dancers. Join us for a toe-tapping, boot-stomping good time, and become a part of the Locust Line & Swing Society family today!
locust-line-swing-society.how_to_get_involved: Join our Instagram page, GroupMe, and come to our events! Events will be announced on our Instagram/GroupMe, with regular sessions returning in the Spring.

adventist-students-for-christ.name: Adventist Students for Christ
adventist-students-for-christ.description: Adventist Students for Christ is a student-led Seventh-Day Adventist Christian group that focuses on both studying the Bible through weekly group discussions and developing strong relationships in fellowship among students, staff, and the large Penn community. Our meetings happen every Friday from 7-8PM (location TBD for Fall/2025). We also host many programs throughout the semester such as fun hangouts, dinners, conferences, end of semester celebration, and more. What we all have in common is LOVE: We love to have fun, we love the Lord, and we love meeting new people! Keep an eye on our Instagram and Facebook pages for events and updates. We are looking forward to meeting you!
adventist-students-for-christ.how_to_get_involved: Right now, you can get involved by joining our Bible study meetings / hangouts on Fridays. We are also planning community-based volunteering activities and other social events for the 2025-2026 school year.

penn-outdoors.name: Outdoors Club at Penn
penn-outdoors.description:
This student group brings together people who love the outdoors. We facilitate meeting like minded people, and planning and going on trips. We've got rock climbers, tree-huggers, hikers, bikers, and everything in between. The Outdoors Club is open to anyone in the Penn Community! Come join us for an adventure anytime!
We meet weekly to debrief past trips, plan future trips, do silly activities, and often eat snacks :) We also offer opportunities to learn outdoor skills throughout the year, and have events on and off campus to get people connected and touching grass!
penn-outdoors.how_to_get_involved:
Join Our Listserve to recieve our weekly emails and pop by our GBM's, every Wednesday at 9PM (Annenberg Plaza). 
Also, join the UPOC GroupMe. This is where club members communicate spontaneous outdoor adventures!

west-philadelphia-tutoring-project.name: West Philadelphia Tutoring Project
west-philadelphia-tutoring-project.description:
WPTP is a program of Civic House that pairs Penn tutors with elementary, middle and high school students for free, one-on-one tutoring services. Tutors cultivate a relationship with their tutee, facilitate academic enrichment, and engage in social justice learning throughout the semester. We are a student group at the University of Pennsylvania.
For Fall 2026, virtual AND in-person tutoring at schools and at Civic House (3914 Locust Walk) will be available.
west-philadelphia-tutoring-project.how_to_get_involved: The Fall 2026 Tutor Application will open in the upcoming weeks. The application deadline is September 11th. Afterwards, we will be accepting applications on a rolling basis until October 20th. We will do our best to find you a time slot!

css.name: Computer Science Society at Penn
css.description: The Computer Science Society is the University of Pennsylvania's computer science student organization. We look to build a community within computer science, and we work to provide students with as many opportunities as we can. Whether we're planning late night cookies, interview prep panels, or hackjams, we're always looking to help out the students and to promote the department.
css.how_to_get_involved: There’s no application required to become a general member — simply request membership on our club page. We look forward to seeing you at our future events!

biomedical-engineering-society-bmes.name: Biomedical Engineering Society (BMES)
biomedical-engineering-society-bmes.description: The Biomedical Engineering Society (BMES) is the undergraduate professional society for the bioengineering department. We serve as a liaison between the faculty and the students, organize social events for BE students to find community outside of the classroom, and host career and networking events.
biomedical-engineering-society-bmes.how_to_get_involved:
Our recruiting process for Fall 2026 will begin soon, so stay tuned!
Join our listserv here: https://forms.gle/guRWAPgK9Ansz62i8

blackgen-capital.name: BlackGen Capital
blackgen-capital.description:
ABOUT US
BlackGen Capital is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. The purpose of BlackGen Capital is to empower underrepresented minorities, specifically Black/African-American, Hispanic, and Native American students, to pursue careers in finance and business by fostering a supportive community and providing accessible educational resources and networking opportunities. We are open to all students. Our focus is to not only cater to students who already have exposure to this industry but to also attract students who do not have any experience with finance and are highly interested in learning more.
CORE VALUES
BlackGen Capital holds four critically important values: Diversity, Empowerment, Philanthropy, and Education.
blackgen-capital.how_to_get_involved: For questions about the club or the recruitment process, please email bgcupenn@gmail.com or the Co-Presidents Gabriel Ray (rayg06@wharton.upenn.edu) and Kelechi Onyia (kelonyia@wharton.upenn.edu)

keynotes-a-cappella.name: Keynotes A Cappella
keynotes-a-cappella.description:
We are a co-ed student a cappella group at the University of Pennsylvania that performs music across pop, indie, alternative, and rock genres. Keynotes is dedicated to fostering musical talent, interdisciplinary community, creativity, and organizational legacy—most notably by exclusively performing original arrangements created by our own members.
Our mission is to share this creativity with others through dynamic performances, group trips that strengthen community, collaborations with fellow musicians beyond Philadelphia, and merchandise that promotes inclusivity and pride. We also record professional albums to preserve our artistry and celebrate the dedication of our members.
keynotes-a-cappella.how_to_get_involved: Fall 2026 open call auditions will be Saturday Aug 29th, and Sunday Aug 30th, from 12pm to 10pm in Williams. You can show up at any time and sign up (in person) for a fifteen minute audition slot! Sign-up sheets will be posted outside the audition room, and please come prepared with a verse and chorus of your favorite song!

prism.name: Programs in Religious, Interfaith, and Spiritual Matters (PRISM)
prism.description: Programs in Religious, Interfaith, and Spiritual Matters (PRISM) cultivates meaningful interfaith relationships on campus by creating opportunities for all students of different traditions, religions, and spiritual backgrounds to connect, share experiences, and learn from one another in a safe and respectful environment.
prism.how_to_get_involved: Reach out! Attend an event (alone or with a friend!), DM us on our Insta (@pennprism), or shoot us an email to get introduced!

180-degrees-consulting.name: 180 Degrees Consulting
180-degrees-consulting.description:
We are a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that consults for social-impact focused businesses. We create value for them through a variety of projects, including new product development, industry research, and marketing campaigns.
Our goal is to strengthen the ability of socially conscious organizations to achieve high-impact social outcomes. We also aim to foster an environment in which consultants can grow as professionals, as individuals, and as a community.
180-degrees-consulting.how_to_get_involved:
180 Degrees Consulting is about making an impact on your community, learning valuable consulting and leadership skills, and working with a fabulous family. We accept students from every major and all four undergraduate schools, and we are excited to learn more about you. Experience is not a prerequisite by any means; we simply care about your interest in learning new things and solving problems! Sign up to our listserv to receive updates on recruitment and reach out to prishav@wharton.upenn.edu or adibala@sas.upenn.edu with any questions!
All of the relevant links for recruiting can be found on our linktree.

society-of-women-engineers-undergraduate.name: Society of Women Engineers (Undergraduate)
society-of-women-engineers-undergraduate.description: The Society of Women Engineers (SWE) at Penn is a collegiate chapter of the national SWE organization, a nonprofit that empowers women to achieve their full potential as engineers and leaders while promoting engineering as a force for positive change. Penn SWE advances this mission through professional development, educational outreach, community building, and advocacy for gender equity. We strive to cultivate an inclusive engineering community in which students can develop professionally, form meaningful connections, support future generations of engineers, and recognize the value of diverse perspectives.
society-of-women-engineers-undergraduate.how_to_get_involved:
All Penn engineers are welcome to attend our events and subscribe to our listserv .
Members seeking a more active role can apply to join one of Penn SWE’s committees:
Advocacy Committee: Promotes gender equity through events for the Penn Engineering community and beyond.
Educational Outreach Committee: Supports STEM education and future generations of women engineers through initiatives such as GEARS Day, High School Shadowing Day, and mentorship with local students.
Community Development Committee: Builds a close-knit, confident community of engineers through social programming, personal connections, and career development.
Fall 2026 committee applications are due September 5 at midnight:
https://forms.gle/bY73gPw2p5pgMDM7A
Board elections are held at the end of the fall semester for calendar-year positions. Students are encouraged to participate in a committee before running for the board.

penn-aerial-robotics.name: Aerial Robotics @ Penn
penn-aerial-robotics.description: Aerial Robotics @ Penn is student-led team at the University of Pennsylvania for the development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and robots. The club aims to provide students with the resources to construct, develop and test their own UAVs, travel to and compete at inter-collegiate competitions, and connect with people who share this same passion. During the 2026-27 school year, we will be designing and constructing micro-class planes, a large high-lift aircraft, and an autonomous tail-sitter VTOL aircraft to compete in 3 separate events at SAE Aero Design 2027. We will also develop a full stack autonomy codebase for a quadcopter robot swarm to compete in IARC, involving computer vision, path planning, and controls.
penn-aerial-robotics.how_to_get_involved: An application is required to join the club. For details, please visit: https://www.pennaerial.com/join-us/

upenn-acm-siggraph-student-chapter.name: ACM SIGGRAPH Student Chapter at Penn
upenn-acm-siggraph-student-chapter.description:
ACM SIGGRAPH Student Chapter at Penn is a computer graphics oriented group which focuses on fostering a community of passionate students interested in animation, computer science, video games, VFX, and graphics in general.
For the upcoming semester in Fall 2026, along with the traditional demo reel/portfolio review night and masterclasses where we bring in alumni from the animation/games industries, we are also implementing an optional project-based curriculum to give students experience with industry standard techniques and software.
upenn-acm-siggraph-student-chapter.how_to_get_involved: To join the mailing list fill out this form. Access our discord using this link :3 And definitely come check us out at the SAC fair!!

alpha-kappa-delta-phi.name: alpha Kappa Delta Phi
alpha-kappa-delta-phi.description: Founded in 1994, the Theta Chapter of alpha Kappa Delta Phi (aKDPhi) at Penn is the first East Coast chapter of the first, largest, and only international Asian-interest sorority. Our organization provides support and sisterhood for all women while promoting awareness of Asian American issues in the University and community.
alpha-kappa-delta-phi.how_to_get_involved: Fall 2026 recruitment events will be in September! Please follow our social media (Instagram) and complete our interest form for updates.

physical-exam-access.name: Physical Exam Access for Community High Schools (PEACH) at Penn
physical-exam-access.description:
PEACH is a student-led organization at the University of Pennsylvania that coordinates with Penn Medicine’s physician event team to provide free and reduced-cost physical exams directly at local high schools. 
This work is powered by Penn undergraduate and medical student volunteers working alongside physicians, at no cost to families. Beyond physicals, PEACH is committed to inspiring and empowering student-athletes. Planned initiatives include partnering with the Netter Center and Penn Athletics to bring students to Penn sporting events, hosting nutrition workshops with hands-on demonstrations, and creating educational opportunities that encourage students to pursue athletics and academics at the next level.
physical-exam-access.how_to_get_involved:
Fill out this interest form: PEACH Volunteer Interest Form 
Feel free to email us at peach.physicalexam@gmail.com with any questions!

kite-and-key.name: Kite and Key Society
kite-and-key.description: Kite and Key is the "handshake of the University," providing tours and other specialized programming for prospective students since 1924. New members go through training during their first semester upon joining, which consists of a day-long Saturday retreat and weekly “Keys Workshops” in which every new member becomes part of a mentor group. We're full of fun-loving, spirited Penn students with a wide range of interests and backgrounds who represent our campus community!
kite-and-key.how_to_get_involved: Applications for Kite & Key's Fall 2026 Training Class open on the first day of classes! Check out the 'Join Kite & Key' tab on our website for more information!

pulj.name: The Undergraduate Law Journal at Penn
pulj.description: A student-run research publication, the Undergraduate Law Journal at Penn (formerly known as PULJ) seeks to foster scholarly discourse on topical and historical issues pertaining to law or the legal system. In this spirit, the journal's principal objective is to publish exceptional undergraduate works, drawn from an array of disciplinary perspectives, that evaluate and elucidate the intricacies, vagaries, and nuances of law as they relate to domestic and international affairs, business, academia, and society. We aims to sustain and enrich a vibrant discussion about law at the undergraduate level because it recognizes that the student writers of today will be the leaders, lawyers, and scholars of tomorrow.
pulj.how_to_get_involved:
Please use this link to join our mailing list!
Please use this link to apply to be in our club. Applications close September 6th at 11:59 PM.

pre-dental.name: Pre-Dental Society
pre-dental.description: The Pre-Dental Society provides programming and a community for undergraduate students at the University of Pennsylvania interested in dentistry and attending dental school. It provides a space for mentorship and discussion regarding being pre-dental at Penn, the Dental Admission Test (DAT), dental school application materials, and dental school in general. Throughout the year, we meet to discuss the direction of the club, organize fundraising opportunities for charitable organizations such as Operation Smile, and partake in volunteer experiences such as assisting with dental hygiene at local primary schools. The Pre-Dental Society connects on a regular basis with students currently in dental school and dentists currently in practice to learn about their journeys to dental school and their career.
pre-dental.how_to_get_involved: Fill out this membership form and email upennpredentalsociety@gmail.com if you have any questions!

the-dream-program.name: DREAM at Penn
the-dream-program.description:
DREAM at Penn is a chapter of Penn students passionate about closing the opportunity gap for low-income households through mentorship. Being a DREAM mentor is a special opportunity to become a long-term safe space in a young person's life and to work alongside a passionate team of peers. We support the development of powerful mentoring relationships with the "Village Mentoring" model, which includes one-on-one and team mentoring. Currently, DREAM@Penn operates at Lucien Blackwell Center. 
DREAM is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit youth services organization that brings high-quality mentoring, adventure, and out-of-school enrichment programs to at-promise youth. Our participants receive quality, no-cost activities that deliver enduring, positive relationships and experiences. Currently, we operate throughout Vermont, Boston, and Philadelphia.
the-dream-program.how_to_get_involved:
We recruit new members on a rolling basis at the beginning of each semester. 
If you are interested in joining DREAM, please fill out this Google Form application : 
After we receive your response, you will be invited to an interview (one round, informal).
If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us at either asantosg@sas.upenn.edu or abbylej@sas.upenn.edu.
We look forward to meeting you!

penn-dhamaka.name: Penn Dhamaka
penn-dhamaka.description: Penn Dhamaka is the University of Pennsylvania’s premier competitive all-male fusion dance troupe, dedicated to celebrating the diversity of South Asian dance and culture through high-energy performances that blend Bhangra, Hip-Hop, Bollywood, Kuthu, Raas, and other dance styles. Our mission is to share our passion for dance, entertainment, and cultural expression with communities across the country while fostering brotherhood, teamwork, and a strong sense of community among our members.
penn-dhamaka.how_to_get_involved:
We are open to all students who share an interest in the above dance styles, or even dance in general!
In addition to their annual show at Penn, Dhamaka travels to competitions at various campuses around the country! Most recently, they competed at and won the Legends National Dance Championship hosted by the Desi Dance Network in Austin!
Stay tuned for details about auditions and look forward to their performances at throughout the year—coming up soon! 
Check out their past performances here: 
Legends 2026: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sCwGDU0esws
Legends 2024: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rmOHpj4MOtI

wax.name: Wharton Asia Exchange
wax.description:
Wharton Asia Exchange (WAX) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. We are a pre-professional community for students who have an interest in the Asia business landscape and are looking to develop their skills in business. 
Our Values
Membership Development: In WAX, our first priority is to be a developmental resource for our members. We strive to make every meeting purposeful and to design events so that members leave having learned something new. 
Diversity (People & Careers): We have hosted Wharton Diversity and Inclusion events and invited Asian speakers to offer advice on issues that are very pertinent to Asian people. 
Community & Support: It's easy to feel lost in a large club. As a result, WAX organizes family groups and smaller social events to make people feel connected in our tight-knit family.
wax.how_to_get_involved:
Learn more about us at SAC fair, Wharton Club fair, or our recruitment events. Apply through our application on PennClubs by September 18th!
Click the bookmark & bell and go to tinyurl.com/waxlistserv to be added to our newsletter!

pennapps.name: PennApps
pennapps.description: Founded in the fall of 2009, PennApps was the nation's first student-run college hackathon. Since then, it has spurred a revolution in the way engineering students develop and showcase their skills, spawning an entire "league" of hackathons across the nation. In past years, over a thousand students from the U.S. and other countries like Switzerland, Canada, England, and Singapore have converged in Philadelphia for the spring and fall editions of the event for a weekend of creation and discovery. Both beginners and experts alike will work together, learn and compete to become better engineers and work on awesome projects.

penn-club-field-hockey.name: Club Field Hockey at Penn
penn-club-field-hockey.description: Club Field Hockey was started at the University of Pennsylvania in 1996 in order to promote the game across the university. We compete in the Central Division of the National Field Hockey League. We have Fall and Spring seasons, which run from September to November and March to April, respectively. During each season, we practice twice a week on the Ellen Vagelos C'90 Field and have one to two games on weekends. Our team is co-ed and members represent undergraduates, exchange students, and graduate students at the University of Pennsylvania. Our team qualified for the National Field Hockey League Fall Championship in 2018 and 2019, advancing to the Top 8 both years. Please check out our instagram @pennclubfieldhockey or contact pennclubfieldhockey@gmail.com for more info!
penn-club-field-hockey.how_to_get_involved:
Please contact our email if you are interested! We take all levels, from complete beginners to former varisty players. Hope to hear from you!
Email: pennclubfieldhockey@gmail.com
Instagram: @pennclubfieldhockey

asian-students-promoting-identity-reflec.name: Asian Students Promoting Identity, Reflection, and Education (ASPIRE)
asian-students-promoting-identity-reflec.description:
The ASPIRE program provides a foundational knowledge of contemporary Asian Pacific Islander American issues for Philadelphia high school students by facilitating open dialogue and identity-based discussions. Our mission is to give participants useful skills such as the ability to analyze and understand current sociopolitical issues and events and the ability to see a more nuanced, inclusive view of America. We also will mentor our participants to help them gain skills they could use for college or other future endeavors and help them utilize the resources available to them.
High school students travel to Penn’s campus twice a month for these 2-hour long, facilitator-led discussions, and receive SEPTA passes for their commute. The program is open to all high school students.
asian-students-promoting-identity-reflec.how_to_get_involved: Let us know if you are interested in becoming a committee member and/or facilitator by emailing us at aspire.upenn@gmail.com! Application form will launch in late August/early September.

beyond-arrests-re-thinking-systematic-op.name: Beyond Arrests: Re-Thinking Systematic-Oppression (BARS)
beyond-arrests-re-thinking-systematic-op.description:
BARS is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania where students engage in dialogues related to criminal justice and anti-carceral advocacy. We frame our agenda around local political action and mutual aid, and hope to generate a continual presence in criminal justice reform, anti-carceral, and abolitionist advocacy in Philadelphia. BARS members evaluate issues at the forefront of criminal justice and advocate for a better world.
Through discussions, workshops, an annual conference, and more, BARS highlights how the criminal justice system disparately impacts different groups and demonstrates the expanse of the carceral state in the US. We often collaborate with other student groups and provide service opportunities for members to be more directly involved with the cause. Finally, BARS often invites speakers to present during our meetings, centering the voices of those who have been incarcerated or who have been impacted by the carceral state.
beyond-arrests-re-thinking-systematic-op.how_to_get_involved: We're always open to new members! Follow and connect with us on our Instagram to receive updates. You can also email us at beyondarrests@gmail.com.

penn-reach.name: REACH at Penn
penn-reach.description:
What is Reach?
Reach at Penn is a student-run club dedicated to creating a community for content creators, digital marketers, and anyone interested in entertainment and social media. 
What do we do?
1. Community - We plan a variety of internal events that are designed to bring our members closer. Ranging from casual game nights to club-wide retreats, we prioritize inclusivity and creating an environment where every member feels well integrated into our club culture.
2. Guest Speakers - From top creators to marketing industry leaders, we bring in speakers to network and learn from the best. 
3. Professional Development (Events) - Through content days, sponsorships, interclub events with other universities, headquarter visitations, we further our members' professional developments within the world of social media.
penn-reach.how_to_get_involved: Our application form is now open! Please apply here: https://forms.gle/ZNemf7wqfV5uMszc6. Applications are due Sept. 20, 2026. Follow our Instagram @upennreach to stay updated with the most accurate information. We do not accept applications via Penn Clubs.

nonprofit-connect.name: Nonprofit Connect
nonprofit-connect.description:
Nonprofit Connect is a student-led program under the Netter Center for Community Partnerships in partnership with the Wharton Undergraduate Division to develop mutually beneficial, collaborative partnerships between Penn students and local nonprofit organizations in the greater Philadelphia area. First piloted in Summer 2020 to address urgent nonprofit needs that emerged during the pandemic, the program continues to connect university resources with community-based organizations through year-long partnerships.
Each academic year, Penn student project teams, led by an upperclassman project manager, and supported by Netter Center student board members, collaborate with nonprofit partners to address short and long-term organizational goals. Through this structure, Nonprofit Connect fosters real-world, community-focused problem solving while helping students gain hands-on experience in project management, communication, and social impact work. The program ultimately aims to strengthen the capacity of local nonprofits while cultivating the next generation of socially-conscious leaders at Penn.
nonprofit-connect.how_to_get_involved:
Member applications for the F26/S27 cohort are now OPEN. 
Fill out the written application here. The last day to apply is September 14th at midnight.
Email nonprofitconnectnetter@gmail.com with any specific questions you have in regards to our program.

nap.name: Nigerians at Penn
nap.description: Nigerians at Penn (NAP) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that strives to connect Nigerians across the University and broader community.
