Membership is open to everyone—you don’t have to be Nigerian to get involved! Whether you identify with Nigeria directly, have roots elsewhere in Africa, or are simply curious to learn more about Nigerian culture, you’ll find a place here. NAP brings people together to celebrate culture, build friendships, and foster growth through speakers, social events, networking opportunities, community outreach, and scholarship.
nap.how_to_get_involved:
Sign up during the club fair, 
Join the Groupme
Request to be a member of the club on Penn Clubs
insta: @nigeriansatpenn; 
Join the NAP board!!

penn-ukrainian-club.name: Ukrainian Student Association
penn-ukrainian-club.description:
Welcome to the Ukrainian Student Association! 
We aim to bring together students of Ukrainian heritage and anyone with an interest in Ukrainian culture at Penn. Our club is open to all undergraduate students, offering a space to celebrate and engage with Ukraine’s rich traditions and history. 
Each month, we organize events where members can meet, have fun, and build connections while exploring Ukrainian culture. We also host discussions on a wide range of topics, including current news, politics, business, and historical developments in Ukraine. 
We try to stay engaged with the broader Ukrainian community in Philadelphia by informing members of upcoming events around the city and even occasionally collaborating!
“Ласкаво просимо до нашого клубу!” (Welcome to our club!)
penn-ukrainian-club.how_to_get_involved: Join our Telegram to chat with fellow members and stay up to date on events! >> https://t.me/+Z2X3yzuZFaE2NGNi

wharton-undergraduate-private-equity-ven.name: Wharton Undergraduate Private Equity & Venture Capital Club (PEVC)
wharton-undergraduate-private-equity-ven.description: We are Wharton's premier student investment club focused on education and engagement surrounding the buy-side. We uniquely combine rigorous investment education with direct access to high-profile finance professionals through speaker sessions and intimate dinners, alongside hands-on experience through pro bono valuations and investment projects. This differentiated platform has helped PEVC achieve near-100% placement into top buy-side roles while fostering a community built around learning, relationships, and real-world impact.

wharton-women.name: Wharton Women
wharton-women.description:
Wharton Women is a student organization open to all undergraduate students at the University of Pennsylvania. Wharton Women facilitates the personal and career development of women and underrepresented gender identities in business by building a network of exceptional undergraduates, professionals and faculty.
Wharton Women aims to provide direction, insight, and camaraderie to women from all four of Penn's undergraduate schools who are interested in business or intend to enter the business world upon graduation. We recieved the Culture of Care Award in 2026 and were voted Wharton's Best Large Club in 2021. Our organization helps members build valuable industry connections through a range of cornerstone events and initiatives, including career panels with industry professionals, workshops on social and professional skills, philanthropic events, and more.
wharton-women.how_to_get_involved: Join our listserv (or subscribe using the bell in top right corner) to come to any and all events and be a General Body Member! To get involved with planning our cornerstone events or other initiatives, apply to be a committee member on the Wharton centralized application in the fall or spring (pennclubs.com/apply). Board positions require one interview and open every December. Students from all schools are invited to get involved.

consult-for-america.name: Consult For America (CFA)
consult-for-america.description:
About Us
We are Consult for America (CFA), a student group at the University of Pennsylvania committed to helping both local entrepreneurs and students reach their maximum business and professional potential. We offering pro-bono consulting services to small businesses, startups, and nonprofits in Philadelphia, and we provide Penn students with the opportunity to cultivate their consulting skills and deepen their community involvement.
History
Founded in 2012, we at Consult for America have been actively serving the Philadelphia community for over a decade. 
From nonprofits to startups to small businesses, we’ve provided strategic perspectives and know-how to a wide variety of clients. Whether you are looking to expand your business, rebrand your product, or are seeking assistance or advice on what to do next, we’re here to help.
http://www.consultforamericaupenn.com
consult-for-america.how_to_get_involved: We recruit a new class of ACs (Associate Consultants) at the beginning of each semester. CFA values and champions diversity of thought, ideas, interests, and passions, and we DO NOT expect applicants to have had any prior experience with consulting. Our application is now live on our Listserv and Instagram and can be accessed through this link: https://forms.gle/NGF1eTaPvunV89Bw5. Please note that applications will be accepted through both Penn Clubs and Google Forms!

pubs.name: Penn Undergraduate Biotech Society (PUBS)
pubs.description:
Penn Undergraduate Biotech Society (PUBS) is the premier student group for undergraduates interested in the intersection between biotechnology, healthcare, and business. We believe in spreading knowledge and excitement about the industry above all else, and we hope that our resources lead to increased awareness about this growing field.
Consulting: This committee provides pro-bono consulting services, advising biotech clients ranging from startups to Fortune 500 companies.
Past Clients: Carisma Therapeutics, Centivax, GlaxoSmithKline, Johnson & Johnson, Merck, Pfizer
Finance: This committee introduces financial concepts within biotech and healthcare, researching markets and crafting investment theses.
Podcast: This committee produces content exploring trends, challenges, and breakthroughs in biotech, featuring industry leaders and academics.
Past Guests: CEO @ Penn Medicine, CEO @ Peptilogics, CSO @ Canomiks, CSO @ L'Oréal, Deputy CMO @ NIH
Research: This committee analyzes emerging scientific literature and novel technologies, collaborating on peer reviews and publications.
If you would like to get involved, please subscribe to our listserv. 
If you have additional questions, please email us at: upenn.pubs@gmail.com.

pds.name: Debate Society
pds.description: As a student group at the University of Pennsylvania, we field teams to over fifteen tournaments per semester, including the World University Debate Championships and topping off our season in the spring with the American Parliamentary National Tournament. In addition to competing, we also host college and high school debate tournaments that attract hundreds of debaters from universities and high schools across the nation. Over the course of the year, we have accumulated several accolades including: top speaker awards, top novice and varsity team finishes, and multiple national qualifiers.
pds.how_to_get_involved: Fall Recruitment is now open! Fill out the application here: https://forms.gle/D1UX3i4HMwGp8TLc9 . The deadline is September 6th, 11:59 PM. Please refer to our website or instagram page for more information. The process will consists of a written application and a virtual interview. If you have any questions, please direct them at cltsao@sas.upenn.edu

pcc.name: Common Cents
pcc.description:
Common Cents is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania and a national nonprofit seeking to empower college & underserved high school students with the knowledge to manage their money and reach financial independence. Our committees work together to hold events and workshops and create educational resources tailored to high school and college students.
Check out our Guide to CC below for more information about our committee
Past Events
pcc.how_to_get_involved:
To join a committee during the Fall and Spring recruitment periods, click the green Apply button at the top of our Penn Clubs page.
To become a GBMer, sign up for our listserv here.

h4i.name: Hack4Impact
h4i.description:
We are the Penn Chapter of Hack4Impact, a student-run 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to developing software for social good. As a Penn student organiztation, we team up with socially-responsible organizations to build products tackling issues in education, food accessibility, poverty, and more. 
Founded in 2014 at Penn, Hack4Impact is one of the earliest tech for good organizations in the country. Since then, Hack4Impact has grown into a national organizations with 10+ university chapters and 800+ members.
h4i.how_to_get_involved:
Check out https://upenn.hack4impact.org/ for more information about who we are, descriptions about roles within Hack4Impact, and why you should join!
Follow us on Instagram (@hack4impactpenn) to stay connected with our community, and If you have any questions or concerns, please email us here: penn@hack4impact.org

boxing.name: Boxing Club at Penn
boxing.description:
Learn to box. Get in shape. Compete. Have fun!
The Boxing Club is a student group at Penn which promotes fitness, mental health, and grit through the study and practice of Western boxing.
We run regular practices focusing on technique and fundamentals, and advanced practices involving more intricate techniques, strategy, and sparring sessions. We welcome all levels of experience, from beginners to competitive boxers. Expect a fun group workout interspersed with partner drills, fighting philosophy, and practical coaching from experienced boxers. Most members are able to spar confidently after one semester with the club!
On the social side, we often hold gatherings such as club dinners and pay-per-view watch parties for the big fights!
If you're looking for a great workout and a great community, join Boxing Club at Penn!
boxing.how_to_get_involved:
The best way to join our club is to attend our first free mega-class, which we host every fall semester schedule coming soon, please follow our Instagram to stay up to date). In this class we will go over the fundamentals of footwork, punching, and movement in boxing. By the end of this first class, you can register for the rest of the semester ($85 for new members, $75 for returning members) to gain access to all of our training sessions and social events.
Questions or concerns? Interested in joining? Drop pennboxing@gmail.com an email anytime.

apsc.name: Asian Pacific Student Coalition (APSC)
apsc.description: Founded in the fall of 1995, the Asian Pacific Student Coalition (APSC) is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania that exists as an alliance of Asian and Pacific Islander (API) student groups. The primary purpose of APSC is to represent the interests and causes of the API community to the University administration. APSC also promotes and celebrates the richness of API culture, facilitates communication between student groups, and provides a forum for discussion on issues of student concern. APSC is open to all members of the University of Pennsylvania and the surrounding community who have an interest in issues relevant to Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders.
apsc.how_to_get_involved:
APSC hosts events throughout the year that all students are welcome to attend. If you would like to be a part of the event planning, political, or marketing committees, our next application will open in the beginning of the Spring semester.
For more information, feel free to contact us at board@upennapsc.com!
Reach out to join our listserv and stay updated with all events among the API community at Penn! Like our page on Facebook and follow us on Instagram (@upennapsc)!

waag.name: Wharton Actuarial & Accounting Group
waag.description: The Wharton Actuarial & Accounting Group (WAAG) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that offers a platform to explore actuarial science and accounting across disciplines and industries, providing a professional network for experiential learning, discovery, and development.
waag.how_to_get_involved: Stay connected and get involved by following our Instagram (@wharton.waag) for the latest updates and insights. Join our listserv to receive important announcements and opportunities directly in your inbox. We encourage you to reach out to our officers for coffee chats to learn more about our club and how you can contribute. Don’t forget to fill out our application—we actively recruit new members during both the Fall and Spring semesters, and we’re excited to see how you can make an impact!

we-can-swim.name: We Can Swim!
we-can-swim.description:
We Can Swim (WCS) provides free swimming lessons to underserved youth, with a particular focus on African American and Hispanic communities that are disproportionately affected by limited access to water safety resources. Our lessons are designed for elementary school students in West Philadelphia, ranging from kindergarten through sixth grade.
We believe that learning essential swimming and water safety skills at a young age is crucial to helping prevent avoidable drownings and promoting lifelong water safety. Through accessible, free swim instruction, WCS strives to equip children with the skills and confidence they need to stay safe in and around the water.
we-can-swim.how_to_get_involved:
Email Us: wecanswimupenn@gmail.com
Volunteer Interest Form: https://forms.gle/B3p1EG4sKqayhPvEA

penn-masti.name: Penn Masti
penn-masti.description: Performing Arts Group: Student group at the University of Pennsylvania
penn-masti.how_to_get_involved:
Check the Penn Masti Instagram and Facebook for updates on auditions. 
Email pennmasti.exec@gmail.com with any questions!

pennsylvania-six-5000.name: Pennsylvania Six-5000 (Penn Six)
pennsylvania-six-5000.description:
Penn Six is Penn's premiere parody comedy acapella group. Just a bunch of people who like to sing, and long walks on the beach... 
We perform A cappella arrangements from all different genres! Sketch comedy included at no additional charge.
We are also a NO AUDITION group, and accept members of all experience levels!
[a student group of the University of Pennsylvania, MDCCXL]
pennsylvania-six-5000.how_to_get_involved: Reach out to us via email fall or spring semesters to get rehearsal info! You can also catch us at activity fairs and A capella auditions (even though we are not auditioning we have a room!). Fill out our interest form to get email updates and information about everything https://forms.gle/VtmRyz1vnskfqor5A :)

south-asian-womens-space.name: South Asian Women's Space
south-asian-womens-space.description: SAWS is a space for all people to build a warm and open community where we feel supported by each other. The group is meant to help students who identify as South Asian at the University of Pennsylvania share experiences and explore their identities, with a focus on the challenges experienced by South Asian women and other marginalized genders. We host discussions and collaborate with other groups while creating meaningful relationships.

wharton-hedge-fund-club.name: Wharton Hedge Fund Club
wharton-hedge-fund-club.description:
Wharton Hedge Fund Club (WHFC) is a premier undergraduate club that seeks to prepare students for personal and professional success in the alternative investments industry. As the sole hedge fund oriented club at the University of Pennsylvania, we have established a diverse base of ambitious and dedicated students passionate about the full range of investing strategies: quantitative finance/macro strategies, commodities, fundamental long/short equity, and more. WHFC's members take part in professional events, stock pitch competitions, career treks, and networking sessions. 
Wharton Hedge Fund Club is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania.
wharton-hedge-fund-club.how_to_get_involved: Please submit an application through Penn Clubs. If applications have closed, we will look forward to reviewing your application next semester. In the mean time, please stay in touch and join our General Body Member (GBM) program here via our listserv.

women-in-computer-science-wics.name: Women in Computer Science (WiCS)
women-in-computer-science-wics.description: Women in Computer Science (WiCS) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that aims to foster a community supporting the advancement of women in tech. Our purpose is to support and promote students who identify as women in CS by encouraging discussion and raising awareness of issues affecting women in computer science. WiCS is open to all students, regardless of gender, gender identity, or sexual orientation, who support the mission of WiCS.
women-in-computer-science-wics.how_to_get_involved:
Our application form for Fall 2026 has opened! 
We will be recruiting for our committees and freshman liaisons: https://forms.gle/Zco7WPoGVfCuyrbN6
Join our email list and check our Instagram to receive updates!! :-)
https://linktr.ee/penn_wics

disney-a-cappella.name: Upstage A Cappella
disney-a-cappella.description: Penn's premier musical a cappella group! Performing the greatest hits from the greatest musicals - Broadway, movies, TV shows, and more! Upstage A Cappella is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania that seeks to spread happiness via musical-theater based songs and service to the community. By performing at hospitals, schools for children, and throughout campus, Upstage A Cappella embodies the joy of song.
disney-a-cappella.how_to_get_involved: Upstage runs auditions with the rest of ACK groups typically at the beginning of each semester. Follow our Instagram page to get updates whenever a new audition cycle begins!

penn-chinese-dance-club-pcdc.name: Chinese Dance Club at Penn (PCDC)
penn-chinese-dance-club-pcdc.description: The Chinese Dance Club at Penn (PCDC) is a student-run, non-profit dance group dedicated to practicing classical and folk chinese dance. Founded in May 2006 as a self-organized group of dance lovers at the University of Pennsylvania, we have flourished into a major performing arts troupe in philadelphia. PCDC’s mission is the enrichment and promotion of traditional chinese arts and culture through dance exercises, instructions, and collaborations. Our club is open to all undergraduate and graduate students.
penn-chinese-dance-club-pcdc.how_to_get_involved: We host workshops and auditions in the fall and spring semesters! Keep up with us on Instagram: @pennchinesedanceclub

the-penn-museum-graduate-advisory-counci.name: The Penn Museum Graduate Advisory Council
the-penn-museum-graduate-advisory-counci.description:
PMGAC Mission
The Penn Museum Graduate Advisory Council (GAC) is a representative council and graduate student group dedicated to facilitating lateral engagement among graduate students and promoting their involvement both as collaborative stakeholders within and as advisers to the Penn Museum.
PMGAC Objectives
To develop and maintain inclusive representation of graduate students from the various disciplines and departments that engage with the Penn Museum
To facilitate academic, professional, and social opportunities for graduate students within the Penn Museum
To build a collaborative relationship with the Penn Museum
To provide graduate students with a means to advise the Penn Museum on issues of interest to graduate students
To build interdisciplinary relationships among graduate students through the Penn Museum
the-penn-museum-graduate-advisory-counci.how_to_get_involved: Any Penn graduate student interested in opportunities at the Museum is welcome to join PMGAC. Council meetings in Fall 2025 are the first Tuesday of every month during the academic year, and open to any Penn graduate student. Workshops and social programs may require pre-registration. For more information on how to get involved as a graduate student in the Museum, contact PMGAC President Kristina Donnally at kbdonn@sas.upenn.edu.

medical-emergency-response-team-mert.name: Medical Emergency Response Team (MERT)
medical-emergency-response-team-mert.description: The Medical Emergency Response Team (MERT) at the University of Pennsylvania is a student-run service organization providing emergency medical services to the University community. The primary purpose of the organization is to complement the emergency medical care provided by the University of Pennsylvania Police Department (UPPD) and the Philadelphia Fire Department (PFD) by providing professional, timely, and high-quality pre-hospital treatment. The secondary purpose of the organization is to provide training and education to students and the community. For more information on MERT, what we do, and how you can join, please visit pennmert.org.
medical-emergency-response-team-mert.how_to_get_involved:
There are two pathways to join MERT:
------------------------------------------
Reciprocity:
If you hold a current EMT certification from any US state (including NREMT), you are eligible to apply to MERT through our Fall 2026 reciprocity application process. 
If you are currently in an EMT class that has not yet concluded, you may be eligible to submit the application for membership through reciprocity. However, you must successfully complete your EMT class and any cognitive/psychomotor examinations required to obtain your certification by September 19th, 2026. Failure to meet this deadline will result in the loss of eligibility for MERT membership through reciprocity for the Fall 2026 application cycle.
Reciprocity applications will be released at 4:00 PM on Sunday, August 30th, and will be due by 11:59 PM on Thursday, September 10th. Late applications will not be accepted. 
------------------------------------------
Spring 2027 EMT Class:
If you do not currently hold an EMT certification, are in your freshman or sophomore year, and would like to certify through MERT, you are eligible to apply to MERT through our Spring 2027 EMT Class application process. 
Applications will be released at 4:00 PM on Sunday, August 30th, and will be due by 11:59 PM on Friday, September 25th. Late applications will not be accepted.
------------------------------------------
Information Sessions
In order to receive an application to MERT, we ask that you attend one of our information sessions:
Saturday, August 29th, 2-3 PM, in person at JMHH F95
Sunday, August 30th, 2-3 PM, virtually on Zoom (please fill out the 2026 MERT Interest Form to receive the Zoom link).
------------------------------------------
If you are unable to attend either information session due to extenuating circumstances, please email membership@pennmert.org.
To receive email updates on the application process and to receive the application form once it is released, please fill out the 2026 MERT Interest Form.
------------------------------------------
Questions? For more information, please visit our website and follow our Instagram (@pennmert) for updates. Please send any questions to membership@pennmert.org.

wharton-korea-undergraduate-business-soc.name: Wharton Korea Undergraduate Business Society
wharton-korea-undergraduate-business-soc.description:
Founded in 2011, W-KUBS is an official, Wharton-recognized student organization fostering a strong, supportive Korea-focused community at Penn and beyond. We educate students on professional and career development and serve as a bridge between business professionals and students.
W-KUBS is composed of 7 committees:
External: Plans premier events, including career treks, speaker series, and MBA networking sessions, while building alumni and corporate relationships.
Professional Development: Runs core pre-professional programming to build recruiting and career readiness skills.
Internal: Fosters camaraderie through monthly socials, joint events with other Korean organizations, and the big/little program.
Consulting: Educates members on consulting careers through workshops and panels.
Business Analysis: Prepares sophomores for finance recruiting through technical training and mock interviews.
Marketing: Manages branding, website, social media, and promotional content.
BBB: Leads our flagship Business Black Box Case Competition, connecting Korean high schoolers with real-world business problem solving.
GBM: Grants access to all events.
wharton-korea-undergraduate-business-soc.how_to_get_involved:
Applications for Fall 2026 are open now. We follow Wharton Council's timeline. 
.
Please direct any questions to both Eric Yoon (ericyoon@wharton.upenn.edu) and Isaiah Chung (ichung32@wharton.upenn.edu), or email whartonkubs@gmail.com

penn-african-students-association.name: African Student Association at Penn
penn-african-students-association.description: African Students Association is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania that strives to educate and promote awareness of Africa in the Penn community. You do not need to be African to join! We are looking to welcome everyone from Penn students who live in Africa, to African students who live in the United States, to Penn students looking to broaden their horizons. The history of Africa and it's heritage is rich and we are open to anyone who is interested in learning about and experiencing African culture!
penn-african-students-association.how_to_get_involved:
If you would like to be added to the listserv, feel free to send us an email.
Follow us on Instagram and stay tuned for more information on upcoming events!

pennaach.name: PENNaach
pennaach.description:
PENNaach, the University of Pennsylvania's premier South Asian Dance Troupe was founded in 1997 to promote South Asian culture through forms of traditional, classical and modern dance. Naach is the oldest surviving Indian fusion dance team in the country. 
PENNaach's unique pieces fuse South Asian dance styles with Western dance styles. 
The team performs in competitions and showcases both on and off-campus. An annual show each February presents self-choreographed pieces with styles from Bharatnatyam and Kathak to Garba and Bhangra to Modern Bollywood and Hip Hop and much more. Dancers on the team have the opportunity to learn many different dance styles as a result. 
PENNaach is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania
pennaach.how_to_get_involved:
Check out our Instagram @pennaach for what we've been up to and our YouTube page for past show videos! Auditions are held in the Fall and Spring - dancers and non-dancers are welcome!
Email pennaach@gmail.com if you have any questions!

nursing-students-for-global-health-nsgh.name: Nursing Students for Global Health (NSGH)
nursing-students-for-global-health-nsgh.description:
Nursing Students for Global Health Club (NSGH) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to fostering a sense of global responsibility and promoting the values of community service, student resources, networking, education, and awareness. Our mission is to engage and serve communities within the Philadelphia area and across the world through a commitment to community service.
What We Offer:
Community Service: NSGH commits to engaging and servicing communities within the Philadelphia area and international communities across the world. 
Student Resources & Networking: NSGH will offer potential opportunities and resources to further engage them in global health education, such as study abroad options, lectures featuring topics of global health, and student panels.
Education & Awareness: NSGH will work to educate the greater Penn student community on the cultures, practices, and healthcare needs most pertinent to diverse sets of people across the globe
nursing-students-for-global-health-nsgh.how_to_get_involved: Membership to join NSGH and attend our events will always be open to everyone. To get involved with various committees, please email us: nsghboard@gmail.com

student-planning-association.name: Student Planning Association (SPA)
student-planning-association.description: The Student Planning Association (SPA) is the University of Pennsylvania’s official Planning Student Organization (PSO) and a pre-professional student group registered with the American Planning Association (APA). SPA fosters an inclusive, interdisciplinary community for students interested in planning and urban affairs across the Weitzman School of Design and the University of Pennsylvania. Through professional development, shared resources, and open dialogue, SPA supports learning, collaboration, and critical engagement with planning practice, policy, and equity.
student-planning-association.how_to_get_involved: Events are open to the public and membership is available to all university students.

penn-hype.name: Hype Dance Crew at Penn
penn-hype.description: Hype Dance Crew is a SAC-sponsored, co-ed, hip hop fusion student dance team at the University of Pennsylvania that creatively and uniquely explores various styles of traditional and modern dance. Established in 2005, Hype is comprised of members from various backgrounds, and aims to bridge cultural divides through the fusion of diverse dance styles.
penn-hype.how_to_get_involved: To receive information about our upcoming auditions fill out the interest form on our website: https://hypedancecrew.com/join. We'll also be posting updates and information on our Instagram @pennhype.

penny-loafers.name: Penny Loafers A Cappella
penny-loafers.description:
Founded in 1986, the Penny Loafers, or Loaf, is the University of Pennsylvania’s only all-gender indie-pop a cappella group.
They perform an eclectic mix of songs from your favorite artists and ones you might not have have heard of before -- they love introducing people to new music!
They're also a competition group -- they compete in the International Championship of A Cappella (ICCA) annually. In their first year competing in 2024, they won their quarterfinal and moved onto semifinals.
penny-loafers.how_to_get_involved:
In order to join the group, students audition during open call and attend subsequent callbacks. 
Members are expected to attend 3 rehearsals per week, participate in gigs, perform in our Winter and Spring concerts, and compete with the group in the International Championship of Collegiate A Cappella (ICCAs).

society-of-hispanic-professional-enginee.name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE)
society-of-hispanic-professional-enginee.description:
The University of Pennsylvania student-run chapter of SHPE aims to empower the Hispanic community to realize its fullest potential and to impact the world through STEM awareness, access, support, and development. Our club does a variety of events including social, community service, academic development, and professional development. Our aim is to foster an enviorment where Hispanic engineers and allies may thrive, connect, and learn from one another while advancing their own professional goals. 
Hope you join us!
SHPE Familia
society-of-hispanic-professional-enginee.how_to_get_involved: Come to our general body meetings once a month! Check out our instagram, mailing list, or website to stay up to date with our events, or shoot us an email if you're wondering what events we've got coming up!

rangoli.name: Rangoli
rangoli.description: Rangoli, the South Asian Association at Penn is a University of Pennsylvania student group that was formed to prolong our culture and rekindle the spirit of various Indian traditions and festivals with verve and vigor. Rangoli is proud to embark upon its twenty-fourth year as it continues to be one of Penn's completely incorporated organizations. We are open to every member of Penn's community as we try to reach out to the various other cultural groups. Rangoli is supported by the Graduate and Professional Student Assembly.

student-committee-on-undergraduate-educa.name: The Student Committee on Undergraduate Education (SCUE)
student-committee-on-undergraduate-educa.description: SCUE seeks to address any issue that affects undergraduate education and the intellectual atmosphere at Penn. We work to enhance and expand curricular opportunities, advising, academic options, and the overall quality of the undergraduate academic experience. We serve our duty as advocates for the student body and as advisors to the faculty and administration.
student-committee-on-undergraduate-educa.how_to_get_involved: SCUE takes new members from all class years every spring and fall semester. Our Instagram, @scue.upenn, has the most up to date timelines!

christian-union-at-penn-formerly-pennfa.name: Christian Union Martus
christian-union-at-penn-formerly-pennfa.description:
Christian Union (CU) Martus is a Christian club at Penn dedicated to growing Christian leadership and faith on campus. We hold to three core values: seeking the Lord wholeheartedly, staying rooted in Scripture, and developing leaders to transform culture. Our weekly activities include prayer, Bible courses, worship nights, and socials. Ministry teams create space for growth through bible study groups and Philia (worship nights and guest speakers). Students also join in retreats, outreach on and around campus, and fellowship events like movie nights or Phillies games.
Whether you are new to Christianity or looking to grow deeper in your walk with God, we would love for you to join us! Please reach out if you are interested in pursuing the Lord with a faithful community of believers at Penn.
christian-union-at-penn-formerly-pennfa.how_to_get_involved: The best way to get involved is to fill out this Interest Form and join our Slack!

upenn-mma.name: MMA At Penn
upenn-mma.description: MMA at Penn is a student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania that provides students with safe, structured, and accessible opportunities to train in mixed martial arts through qualified coaching, appropriate equipment, dedicated training space, and protective flooring and mats. The organization also seeks to support student participation in sanctioned competitions by helping cover registration fees, travel-related expenses, and other costs necessary for competitive development.
upenn-mma.how_to_get_involved:
Instagram Page: https://instagram.com/penn_mma/
Announcements Chat: https://web.groupme.com/join_group/96649657/U6qGTBPy
join the groupme for all updates!

pennchants.name: The Pennchants
pennchants.description:
The Pennchants are the University of Pennsylvania's premier all-male a cappella group.
A highly professional student-run group that balances touring, recording, and high-profile performances, the Pennchants have earned widespread recognition as a group that delivers fresh energy and never fails to win over audiences' hearts with their distinct blend of pop, rock, and the songs of our childhood. The members pride themselves on their innovative concerts, iconic brand, and close sense of community. It's truly a group that does it all. 
The Pennchants perform one large-scale concert per semester, collaborating with their sister group, The Quaker Notes, in the fall. The Pennchants are also known for their hands on start-to finish production process, giving new members the opportunity to learn video and audio editing from senior members.
The Pennchants are officially sponsored by the MEMBERS ONLY brand.
pennchants.how_to_get_involved: Fill out our audition interest form or reach out to us with any questions you may have. Open auditions this semester are on August 29th and 30th! More announcements can be found on our social media. Just type "The Pennchants" on any platform and you should be able to find us!

zeta-phi-beta-sorority-inc.name: Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Inc.
zeta-phi-beta-sorority-inc.description: Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Inc. was founded on January 16, 1920, at Howard University in Washington, D.C. Since its inception, Zeta has continued its steady climb into the national spotlight with programs designed to demonstrate concern for the human condition both nationally and internationally. As our sorority reaches its centennial year, it retains its original zest for excellence. It espouses the highest academic ideals and that has resulted in its members serving in groundbreaking roles in all fields of endeavor. Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Inc. is poised for perpetual service to mankind into her second century and beyond. The Mu Iota Chapter was founded on May 19, 1979 on the campus of the University of Pennsylvania. We are a collective student group of collegiate women at the University of Pennsylvania who are looking to add more members to the sisterhood!

penn-heroes.name: Penn Heroes
penn-heroes.description:
Penn Heroes is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. Our goal is to cheer up patients and raise money for those in need, whether through volunteering, fundraising, or design efforts in conjunction with different hospitals and organizations.
The commitment level for Penn Heroes is totally up to you! You can represent us as a hospital volunteer, lead in a fundraiser, or create videos/cards to cheer up a patient in need. Whether you want to raise money, race for people's health, visit hospitals and patients weekly, or just make fun content, we would love to have you with us!
penn-heroes.how_to_get_involved: Join our newsletter at http://eepurl.com/iIPkpY Email us at upennheroes@gmail.com with any questions.

quest-scholars-at-penn.name: QuestBridge Scholars at Penn
quest-scholars-at-penn.description:
Quest Scholars at Penn is a campus chapter of QuestBridge Scholars Network (QSN), a national community for individuals who were both selected as National College Match Finalists and attend QuestBridge college partners. This student-run group brings QuestBridge Scholars at Penn together to foster a stronger community and personal relationships, advocate for their needs, and provide all support necessary to allow QuestBridge Scholars thrive.
Our mission is not only to build a supportive and welcoming community for first-generation and low-income students, but also cultivate relationships with other groups and services to support our members. As a chapter, we provide support and offer growth, service and leadership opportunities. By collaborating with other FGLI organizations and Penn administrators, the group offers various events that cover everything from career and academics to social life and mentorship.
quest-scholars-at-penn.how_to_get_involved: Though there are no requirements, we expect that members will attend as many events as they can.

quakerbots.name: QuakerBots
quakerbots.description: QuakerBots is a student group at Penn, and its first combat robotics team, where we build robots to fight in competitions across the country, such as NHRL or GSRL, as well as hosting and attending local robotics events. We don't require any experience to join, and have programs to teach the skills we use to build our robots. Join if you want to have fun with robots, learn engineering skills, and enable carnage in the ring!

growth-equity-at-penn.name: Wharton Undergraduate Growth Equity
growth-equity-at-penn.description: Welcome to Wharton Undergraduate Growth Equity the University of Pennsylvania's premier undergraduate growth equity club. We are dedicated to fostering deep interest and expertise in the growth equity industry, with a focus on software investing. Our mission is to offer students unparalleled opportunities to master the intricacies of growth equity investing, acquire hands-on experience through real-world projects, and gain valuable recruiting insights.
growth-equity-at-penn.how_to_get_involved: Interested in joining Wharton Undergraduate Growth Equity? Keep an eye out for our application cycle each semester, typically in the fall. Get involved by subscribing to our listserv for updates on future opportunities. Our comprehensive programs, including the Growth Equity Accelerator and Practicum, offer students hands-on experience, recruitment prep, and networking with top industry professionals. Don't miss your chance to dive into the world of growth equity!

upenn-math-contest.name: Math Contest at Penn
upenn-math-contest.description:
Math Contest at Penn is a student organization dedicated to hosting an annual math contest for high school participants. Our student group is focused on expanding mathematical outreach and stoking high school students' interest in math. There are many positions that don't require mathematical knowledge, such as social media, finance, logistics, and day-of volunteering. Please feel free to reach out to us with questions on how to get involved!
Our club is dedicated to spreading a passion for mathematics to students of all levels. As such, last year we ran both a beginner and an advanced contest to reach a broader audience of students. We included diverse mathematical problems from high school algebra, geometry, combinatorics, logic, and other fields, and we are always welcoming more ideas on how the contest should be run to make it appealing and exciting for students!
upenn-math-contest.how_to_get_involved:
If you have any questions, feel free to send us an email!
Also, why not follow our Instagram account while you're at it? https://instagram.com/pennmathcontest/

advocates-for-neurodiversity-and.name: Advocates for Neurodiversity (AND)
advocates-for-neurodiversity-and.description: AND is a student organization focused on neurodiversity at Penn. We aim to bring broader awareness to neurodivergence, support the neurodiverse student population, and create a cultural space for Neurodivergents on campus. We host workshops, social events, and awareness campaigns to make Neurodivergent culture a part of Penn's diverse campus. Students of all neurotypes are welcome to join!

penn-italian-club.name: The Italian Club at Penn
penn-italian-club.description: The Italian Club @ Penn is the premier community for Penn students interested in all things Italian. We welcome students with a diverse range of cultural experiences and language ability, with a deep interest in Italian culture. No proficiency in the Italian language is required! But we will help you achieve confidence in your Italian skills. We collaborate with the Italian Department and host a number of events both in and off campus.
penn-italian-club.how_to_get_involved: We are always accepting new general members! You can join our mailing list here.

unicef.name: UNICEF at Penn
unicef.description:
UNICEF at Penn is a student-led organization dedicated to advancing the rights and well-being of children, in Philadelphia and around the world. Guided by UNICEF's mandate from the United Nations General Assembly, we work to ensure every child has access to health, protection, education, and opportunity.
We pursue this mission through four pillars. We fundraise to support UNICEF's global programs and to sustain the campus programming, partnerships, and operations that make our work possible. We advocate for children's issues at the local, state, national, and international levels. We serve and build community, partnering with organizations across Penn and Philadelphia and developing our members as informed, capable leaders. We educate our peers on the challenges shaping children's lives, including public health, humanitarian crisis, displacement, inequality, and exploitation.
Together these pillars build lasting capacity within our chapter, on our campus, and in the communities we serve.
unicef.how_to_get_involved:
Please fill out this interest form and application to join our Fall 2026 email list (and learn more about our events) : 
UNICEF at Penn Interest Form Link
UNICEF at Penn Committee Application Link 
UNICEF at Penn Leadership Application Link
Application Timeline:
Both Application Are Due: September 4, 2026
Committee Application Results: Week of September 7th
Leadership Interviews: Week of September 7th

honor-council.name: University Honor Council
honor-council.description:
The University Honor Council of the University of Pennsylvania (UHC) is an undergraduate student body that promotes academic integrity and honorable conduct in the Penn community. Working closely with the Center for Community Standards and Accountability, we run several initiatives to this end. Moreover, members of the UHC send representatives to sit on student conduct hearings.
The UHC actively lobbies all parts of the University to promote academic integrity and ethical conduct. We strive to achieve these by educating fellow students via various campaigns and presentations. In addition, we serve as members of the judicial board for undergraduate academic integrity and conduct-related affairs. We are independent from all other student groups, and receive funding and support through the Office of the Provost.
honor-council.how_to_get_involved:
Follow us on Instagram @pennuhc to find recruitment information! 
Interest Form here: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfdoAxLHFsZY0lpsXtS7PXQRo9CohiFpuD7W_gOfY5d3YJK_w/viewform?usp=dialog

penn-in-hand.name: Penn-In-Hand
penn-in-hand.description: We are Penn’s first and only student organization for American Sign Language and Deaf Culture. Our mission is to give students the opportunity to strengthen their ASL skills while engaging meaningfully with the Deaf community through hosting events throughout the semester. We welcome members of all signing abilities by hosting Crash-Course ASL lessons for beginners, social hours for those with more ASL experience, and a plethora of other ways to educate our campus about Deaf culture. There is no membership requirement to be a part of our club — Deaf, hearing, and all levels of signing knowledge are welcome to our events!
penn-in-hand.how_to_get_involved:
There are many ways to become involved in Penn-In-Hand! First and foremost, join our mailing list, our Groupme, and follow us on Instagram (@penninhand) to hear about our events! Event RSVPs will also be added to our Linktree, which can be found in our Instagram bio. Penn also offers introductory ASL courses. More information about the ASL and Deaf Studies department can be found here. 
Interested in becoming a member of Board? Reach out to penninhand.upenn@gmail.com and CC our presidents Anya Stewart (anyab19@engineering.upenn.edu) and Grace Melone (melone24@nursing.upenn.edu) detailing your interest and experience!

penn-chinese-theater.name: Chinese Theater at Penn
penn-chinese-theater.description: Founded in 2013, Chinese Theater at Penn is the only student-run theater group at Penn that is dedicated to providing a stage for Chinese and Asian cultural heritage. Ranging from thrill, historical, to musical, CT's production in each semester adapts one Chinese theatrical masterpiece, letting the Penn audience explore the art of comedy and tragedy. Our mission is to bring our audience the beauty and charm of Chinese drama, and we aim to deliver high-quality Chinese theatrical plays to the Penn community.
penn-chinese-theater.how_to_get_involved: More to be released on Instagram and WeChat official account (宾大中文戏剧社，pennct2013)

aspiring-educators-at-penn.name: Aspiring Educators at Penn
aspiring-educators-at-penn.description: Aspiring Educators at Penn is a community of undergraduate students interested in the field of education. We provide mentorship opportunities, social events, and academic and career resources. The goal of Aspiring Educators at Penn is to connect undergraduate students interested in the field of education and to provide a space for students to explore careers in the field with a particular focus on the teaching profession.
aspiring-educators-at-penn.how_to_get_involved:
To become a recognized member of Aspiring Educators, fill out our membership form: https://forms.gle/uTbJSnQAfiL5k8Zd7
To receive our newsletter, fill out our interest form: https://forms.gle/AQeA16pdg9njruSC7 
If you have any questions, contact: aspiringeducatorsatpenn@gmail.com

asian-pacific-athlete-coalition.name: Asian Pacific Indigenous Athlete Coalition (APIAC)
asian-pacific-athlete-coalition.description: The Asian Pacific Indigenous Athlete Coalition exists to empower athletes of Asian, Pacific Islander, and Indigenous heritage by fostering community, amplifying diverse voices, and celebrating shared histories. We are committed to advancing equity in sports and creating inclusive spaces where culture and identity are honored. In addition to creating a social space for discussing a shared identity, we also work with the West Philadelphia area through philanthropic events. Our club is open to anyone who aligns with our mission and would be interested in joining!
asian-pacific-athlete-coalition.how_to_get_involved: Apply through Penn Clubs or show up to one of our events!

global-research-and-consulting.name: Global Research and Consulting (GRC)
global-research-and-consulting.description:
The Global Research and Consulting (GRC) Group at Wharton is a dynamic, student-run consulting organization dedicated to giving students substantive, real-world problem-solving experience. 
Our mission is to bring together the most talented, passionate, and diverse students from around the world, forge them into a tight-knit community, and empower them to deliver exceptional results for our global clients.
We provide research and strategy consulting to industry-leading organizations across the consumer, financial services, healthcare, technology, and nonprofit sectors, including Google, Johnson & Johnson, Microsoft, WWF, and NASA. We are committed to developing rigorous, collaborative future leaders and to sustaining a community that supports its members well beyond graduation.
global-research-and-consulting.how_to_get_involved:
For all the latest news from GRC, sign up for our listserv here! 
Joining GRC
GRC recruits new members each semester through an application and interview process. We hold information sessions and coffee chats beforehand so prospective members can meet the team. No prior consulting experience is required.
What membership looks like
Members join a project team and work directly with a client over the course of the semester, led by a Project Leader. Teams meet weekly with additional client-facing meetings throughout the engagement.
Beyond client work
- Finance and consulting recruiting preparation
- NYC Career treks to firms including BCG, Bain, Cornerstone
- Case competitions, including our Bain case competition (F'26)
- Social events throughout the year and an end-of-year formal
- An active alumni network across consulting, finance, and industry

penn-aero.name: Aerospace Club @ Penn
penn-aero.description:
The Aerospace Club @ Penn is the University of Pennsylvania’s student community of aerospace engineers, researchers, and enthusiasts. We are one of the most dynamic, fastest growing, and visible student groups at Penn. We offer students a hands-on project oriented experience and guide them towards aerospace technology innovation. 
The club is aims to provide aerospace experience through four subteams' projects that provide their own engineering experience and goals: High-Power Rocket, High-Altitude Balloon, Aircraft Design-Build-Fly, and Jet Propulsion. Each tackles their own engineering and research process, offering valuable technical experience. As the primary aerospace-focused group on campus, the Aerospace Club at Penn is comprised of the best aerospace talent Penn has to offer. We serve a wide audience, with over 150 members, and the club continues to grow every semester with new recruits.
penn-aero.how_to_get_involved:
Applications are currently closed. 
For questions pertaining to specific subteams, please reach out to our team leads:
Co-Directors: Archisa Arora (arora26@engineering.upenn.edu), Cameron Zuschmidt (czusch26@engineering.upenn.edu)
Aircraft: Lana (lastout@engineering.upenn.edu)
Rocket: Kayleen (kss1006@engineering.upenn.edu), Raphael (raphlo@engineering.upenn.edu)
Balloon: Yi Lu Zheng (yzheng6@engineering.upenn.edu) and Sebastian (srod82@engineering.upenn.edu)
Jet Propulsion: Diego (diegosa@engineering.upenn.edu) 
SOCIALS
Stay updated with us on Instagram: @pennaerospace, and check out our website for more information on our individual subteams: aerospaceclub.seas.upenn.edu

penn-effective-altruism.name: Effective Altruism at Penn
penn-effective-altruism.description: Effective Altruism at Penn is a community of Penn students dedicated to using evidence and reason to figure out how to do the most good, and to acting on what we find. We promote high-impact approaches to global health and poverty, animal welfare, and existential risks (such as AI and pandemics) through philanthropy, policy, and careers.
penn-effective-altruism.how_to_get_involved: Join our Slack (bit.ly/eapennslack) and mailing list (eapenn.eo.page/list) to join the club and to stay informed about upcoming events and opportunities! Send us an email at upenneffectivealtruism@gmail.com if you are interested in helping organize or take on a leadership role.

camp-kesem.name: Kesem at Penn
camp-kesem.description: Kesem at Penn is a chapter of the national Kesem organization that supports children through and beyond their parent's cancer. Kesem's flagship program, Camp Kesem, operates free summer camps for children who have been impacted by a parent's cancer. Kesem is the largest national organization dedicated to this unique population, and for many children their Camp Kesem experience is a life-changing event—providing them with a community of children with similar experiences, and a safe and welcoming environment to have fun and rediscover their childhood.
camp-kesem.how_to_get_involved: You can be involved with Kesem as a coordinator, a counselor, or a general body member. Summer camp counselor applications open around winter break. Anyone is welcome to be a general member year-round and those interested in becoming counselors are encouraged to join as general members in the fall.

collective-success.name: Collective Success at Penn
collective-success.description: Collective Success at Penn (CSN @ Penn) is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to empowering first-generation and/or low-income (FGLI) students. We foster professional development and personal growth by connecting students with a supportive network of FGLI professionals and advocates, and by offering mentorship, career-focused meetings, collaborative events with other Collective Success chapters, partnerships with companies and organizations, and programming designed to support career success.

counterparts.name: Counterparts
counterparts.description: Counterparts is Penn’s oldest all gender student a cappella group. Founded in 1981, Counterparts has a repertoire spanning from pop hits to jazz standards - including Etta James' "At Last," hits like Radiohead’s “Creep," and alumnus John Legend’s “Slow Dance" (CP '99).
counterparts.how_to_get_involved: Visit penncounterparts.com/audition and fill out our audition interest form for updates!

university-of-pennsylvania-esports-assoc.name: Esports Club
university-of-pennsylvania-esports-assoc.description:
Esports is student organization at Penn for all gamers–from casual watchers to competitive players alike. Are you interested in competitive shooters like VALORANT, chill RPGs like Honkai Star Rail, or mobile games like Clash Royale? Sign up to be a part of a diverse, welcoming community for undergraduates and graduates.
Our activities include:
Watch parties for your favorite Esports leagues
Casual in-house scrimmages
Travel LAN tournaments
…and much more!
Join our Discord today: https://discord.gg/XCyZJUSCpz

quaker-notes.name: Quaker Notes
quaker-notes.description:
Quaker Notes is the University of Pennsylvania's premier, nationally acclaimed student a cappella group. 
We sing a wide variety of music genres: pop, rock, r&b, and alternative. Our style is entertainment and we are committed to showing our audience a good time. All of our music is arranged by current Quaker Notes and alumnae, and we arrange & learn more than 20 new songs every year! Quaker Notes is for students who are excited about sharing their passion for music and performance, ontributing to a close-knit, community, and exploring creativity through arranging, singing, and performance. Any student at Penn is welcome to audition!
quaker-notes.how_to_get_involved: Follow us on Instagram for the most up-to-date audition announcements!

penn-grey-matters.name: Grey Matters at Penn
penn-grey-matters.description:
We are a student group at Penn continuing Grey Matters, which first started at the University of Washington to broaden access to neuroscience content. At Penn, we embody the very purpose for which Grey Matters was founded. Neuroscience is one of the fastest-growing fields, with rapid developments in brain technology, emotions, and neurodegenerative disease research. It is therefore imperative to broaden access to these interesting yet useful topics. Grey Matters serves as a focal point for neuroscience information that should be widely accessible, not restricted to neuroscience students. We are composed of artists, engineers, writers, and many others across disciplines. Students of any major can write articles and potential research papers for publication on topics intersecting neuroscience. We also provide free podcasts engaging with Penn faculty on research, experiments, and the future of the field. Lastly, we are committed to writing and discussing animal behavior.
https://greymattersjournalpenn.com/
penn-grey-matters.how_to_get_involved: To get involved, check out the following link: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc7I3BGZ3JpGkf5zKyMBuqjDsCq-CwdV8mUsLcb05tBS51ILQ/viewform?usp=preview

umoja.name: UMOJA
umoja.description: UMOJA speaks as the representative voice of Black students and student organizations at the University of Pennsylvania and derives its legitimacy from the consent and confidence of its membership organizations (Constituents). UMOJA is charged with uniting its Constituents into a common political voice, mobilizing its Constituents for a common agenda, and organizing its Constituents under a common calendar. While UMOJA’s mission is rooted in advancing the experiences of Black students, its programs, advocacy, and activities remain open to the entire Penn community.
umoja.how_to_get_involved: UMOJA is a 7B umbrella organization that represents Black constituent groups at Penn. The best way to get involved is by joining a constituent group’s executive board, which provides firsthand experience in how UMOJA operates. Our role includes collecting feedback from our constituents and presenting it to higher entities, as well as providing funding and support to our groups. UMOJA Board applications open in late November, and the newly selected board officially transitions each January. While our focus is on the needs of Black students, all members of the Penn community are welcome to engage with our programming and initiatives.

korean-graduate-students-association.name: Korean Graduate Students Association (KoGSA) at Penn
korean-graduate-students-association.description: Korean Graduate Students Association (KoGSA) was established to promote fellowship among Korean graduate students in various departments. Through social, academic, and cultural events, KoGSA allows students to exchange scholastic and cultural information. Also, KoGSA strives to introduce Korean culture and tradition to the University of Pennsylvania community in collaboration with undergraduate Korean student associations.

cit59x.name: CIT59x
cit59x.description: We are a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that seeks to connect and support MCIT In-Person students through community and professional events.
cit59x.how_to_get_involved: Reach out to the 59x board through Instagram or email club President miabgold@engineering.upenn.edu!

sudanese-association-at-penn.name: Sudanese Association At Penn
sudanese-association-at-penn.description: The Sudanese Association at Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to creating a vibrant and inclusive community that celebrates Sudanese culture and heritage. Our organization welcomes all students who are interested in learning about, engaging with, and supporting the Sudanese community and its allies.
sudanese-association-at-penn.how_to_get_involved: We’ll be recruiting new members at the end of the fall semester! Our membership process is open to all students who are passionate about Sudanese culture or interested in connecting with our community. Keep an eye out for our upcoming events, and feel free to reach out if you’d like to get involved, we’d love to welcome you!!

ghana-grad-society.name: Ghana Graduate Society
ghana-grad-society.description: The Ghana Graduate Society at Penn celebrates and promotes Ghanaian culture, history, and values while building community among graduate students at the University of Pennsylvania—welcoming both Ghanaian students and others interested in Ghana.

f-word.name: F-Word: A Collection of Feminist Voices
f-word.description:
Feminism (noun): Respect for people of all genders, sexualities, and races. 
The F-Word is a collection of feminist voices that comes together in a biannual print publication, weekly discussion groups, and an online blog. We are a student-run publication at the University of Pennsylvania, and we aim to be a space for people of all backgrounds to talk, write, or create art through their experiences. We hope to represent and welcome many voices with meaningful thoughts to share: queer, POC, all genders, and all socioeconomic backgrounds. We hope to foster more thoughtful campus discussion on the bounds of and potential for feminism, intersectionality, social justice, and the role of publication and writing in all of the above.
f-word.how_to_get_involved: Our general membership is open to all Penn students, no applications needed! In order to become a member, all you have to do is attend and participate consistently during our weekly GBMs hosted at Kelly Writers House (specific times and locations vary from semester to semester, check our listerv for meeting information). If you are interested in taking on a more active role with responsibilities in Editorial, Design, or Internal and External Communications, applications are open at the beginning of each semester. You can also subscribe to our listserv here, or follow us on Instagram!

apo.name: Alpha Phi Omega
apo.description: Alpha Phi Omega is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania, and is a national, gender inclusive service fraternity that has set the standard for college campus-based volunteerism since 1925. We strive to help each individual member develop leadership skills, experience friendship on many levels, and provide service to others.
apo.how_to_get_involved:
Attend our rush events at the beginning of the fall and spring semesters. All genders, majors, and years are welcome!
Fall 2026 RUSH INFORMATION:
[ATTEND 1]
Meet & Greet: Meet current brothers and learn about APO over fun ice breakers!
(1) 09/08, (2) 09/10, (3) 09/11
[ATTEND ALL]
Big-Little Mixer, Lellowship, Speed Dating, and Rush Service
**Exact time and locations to be announced on Instagram: @apo_upenn
We understand that schedules can be busy, and we want to ensure everyone has an opportunity to participate. If you’re unable to attend any of the events, please don’t hesitate to email us at apoexec.pledgeds@gmail.com. We’re happy to accommodate!
Please fill out this interest form to be placed on our listserv. 
Fall 2026 Rush Interest Form!

penn-lions.name: Penn Lions
penn-lions.description: Penn Lions is the Greater Philadelphia region's premier collegiate lion dance troupe. The troupe was formed in 2007 as a branch of Chinese Students Association and has since evolved into its own independent student group at Penn. As a student group, we meet practice traditional Chinese Lion dancing and work towards spreading the art of lion dancing throughout the greater Philadelphia area. Since its formation, this student group has performed not only on campus, but all across the East Coast for weddings, a countless number of schools, festivals, TV stations like NBC and ABC, Philadelphia's mayor Michael Nutter, the USMNT, and more!
penn-lions.how_to_get_involved:
Interest Form for 2026-2027 
Join us in performing the art of Chinese lion dance! Our busiest performance season is Lunar New Year, but we train and perform both semesters. Every troupe member will train both in the lion and as a musician. No experience is necessary. Members are expected to attend at least ~70% of practices and are highly encouraged to attend our yearly retreat and the intercollegiate competition.
If you are interested in joining, please enter your email address when subscribing so we can send you recruitment information!

front-row.name: Front Row Theatre Company
front-row.description: Front Row Theatre Company (FTC) is a student-organized theatre company at the University of Pennsylvania. FTC produces theatre that engages with cultural, political, and societal experiences relevant to its membership and its greater communities. FTC is dedicated to bridging our art to local communities by involving its membership in service opportunities in conjunction with each production.
front-row.how_to_get_involved:
We accept new members for every seasonal production (fall, winter, and spring)! No prior experience necessary: whether you're interested in acting, production, technical work, or administration (or some combination of all!) we are always looking for people with a commitment to our mission and a vision to contribute.
We perform a small excerpt from some of our work at Student Performing Arts Night (SPAN) during the first week of the fall term. For more information on auditions, tech interviews, and community service events, please visit our social media pages and/or contact us!

wharton-future-of-cities-conference.name: Wharton-Weitzman Future of Cities Forum
wharton-future-of-cities-conference.description:
The Wharton-Weitzman Future of Cities Forum is an annual convening at the University of Pennsylvania for the people remaking the built environment. Organized by graduate students across the Wharton School and the Weitzman School of Design, the Forum exists on a simple premise: the future of cities gets decided where capital and design meet. Each year, we gather practitioners at the frontier of housing, mobility, climate, and finance to show what they’re building and compare notes on what’s next.
Over seven years, the Forum has convened more than 180 speakers, including four mayors and governors, planning directors, and transit chiefs from New York to Quito — alongside the CEO of Related Companies and leaders from Goldman Sachs, McKinsey, CBRE, Hines, Google X, and Fifth Wall. The Forum has also featured acclaimed urbanists like Richard Florida, Matthew Yglesias, Vishaan Chakrabarti, and Majora Carter.

asian-pacific-american-law-students-asso.name: Asian Pacific American Law Students Association (APALSA)
asian-pacific-american-law-students-asso.description: APALSA supports the professional, academic, and personal development of our members while promoting Asian and Pacific American interests in the legal sphere. Through programming and engagement with the broader legal community, we foster dialogue on critical contemporary legal issues and prepare our members for well-rounded, successful careers. Our keystone event, the annual APALSA Conference (co-hosted with Penn Carey Law's Asian Law Review), brings together students and speakers from across the country to discuss legal issues affecting Asian and Pacific Americans. APALSA is committed to advancing diversity in broad and vibrant ways, including coalition-building and allyship across marginalized and historically underrepresented communities.
asian-pacific-american-law-students-asso.how_to_get_involved: Email president@pennapalsa.org and sign up for the newsletter on pennapalsa.org.

wharton-undergraduate-data-analytics-clu.name: Wharton Undergraduate Data Analytics Club (WUDAC)
wharton-undergraduate-data-analytics-clu.description: The Wharton Undergraduate Data Analytics Club provides Penn undergraduates with the chance to develop data analytics skills, explore career paths in the field of data analytics, network with professionals in data-driven industries, and be a member of a data-focused community at Penn.
wharton-undergraduate-data-analytics-clu.how_to_get_involved:
1) Apply for Analytics 101 or Analytics 201: In Fall 2026, we will be accepting applications for our two workshops: 101 and 201. 
Analytics 101: an introductory program to break into data science, covering topics in exploratory data analysis, probability/statistics, data pre-processing and visualization, and machine learning and deep learning methods. 
Analytics 201: work in teams to analyze and build models for a company on a real-world data analytics project collaboration that spans the semester. 
Note: There is no formal prereq for applying to 201. Generally, most 201 applicants complete 101 beforehand, but there is no official requirement. Also, 201 may followed by one round of interviews.
2) Join committees: In Fall 2026, we will be accepting applications for our Events, Finance, Marketing, and Education committees. Applications may be followed by one round of interviews. Sign up for our listserv here for weekly updates on upcoming events and opportunities!

spec.name: Social Planning and Events Committee (SPEC)
spec.description:
***This is a parent group to our other committees. Please search for "SPEC" within the Penn Clubs system to sign up for an individual committee***
The Social Planning and Events Committee (SPEC) is one of the branch of student governance that is responsible for planning a variety of social events and traditions on campus. There are eight committees under SPEC: Concerts, Connaissance, Film, Jazz & Grooves, Pop Up, Sound, SPEC-TRUM, and Spring Fling (Daytime).
If you have a creative mind and a passion for uniting students with fun and innovative events, you should reach out to any committee or our executive board to join. There is no limit on the number of committees that you can join. No application or interview is needed for any of the committees.
spec.how_to_get_involved:
Look up the committee(s) that you are interested in on Penn Clubs to find their specific information. Joining their listserv or emailing their directors will allow you to receive information about meeting times, sub-chair positions, and more. If you need help getting in contact with a committee, feel free to email exec@specevents.net or direct message @upennspec on Instagram.
Fall 2026: We will be hosting a SPEC-wide info session after the SAC club fair. All committees will be present.

west-philly-swingers.name: West Philly Swingers
west-philly-swingers.description: The West Philly Swingers is UPenn's official swing dancing troupe! Our goals are to have fun, make friends, and learn to dance along the way. We are both a social and a performance group, dancing mainly Lindy Hop and West Coast Swing.
west-philly-swingers.how_to_get_involved:
We have all-levels-welcome auditions every semester! No experience required! We teach a beginner lesson at each audition, and have time to get to know current West Philly Swingers members and other auditionees.
For the Fall 2026 semester we will be having two audition dates which will be released shortly. Reach out at wpswing.captain@gmail.com for any questions!

dischord-a-cappella.name: Dischord A Cappella
dischord-a-cappella.description: Founded in 1998, Dischord is the University of Pennsylvania's premier Pop and R&B all gender A Cappella group. We are student run and perform one show per semester, in addition to a variety of outside gigs. We cover artists like The Weeknd, Billie Eilish, Coldplay, Beyoncé, Mariah Carey, Bruno Mars, and more. Although we are a singing group, we like to say that we are 49% music and 51% family!
dischord-a-cappella.how_to_get_involved: Come out to open auditions in early September! Follow @penndischord on Instagram for the most up-to-date information, or fill out the interest form on our website!

stimulus.name: Stimulus Children's Theatre Company
stimulus.description:
The mission of Stimulus Children’s Theatre Company (Stim) is to produce shows that teach valuable lessons which resonate with audiences of all ages. Students at the University of Pennsylvania share stories that communicate themes we feel are important to pass on to young audiences, such as friendship, acceptance and compassion. 
In addition to performing on-campus shows for our peers (typically a musical in the Fall and a play in the Spring), Stim is unique among Penn student theatre in our community service endeavours. From off-campus community shows to theatre-based workshops, we love to inspire, benefit and teach Philadelphia youth. Our community-based programming draws upon our experiences within theatre and music to provide arts-based enrichment for children in Philadelphia.
stimulus.how_to_get_involved:
Auditions for the Fall 2026 musical will be on 8/29 from 6:30-10:30 PM and 8/30 from 12-4 PM, and tech interviews to join the production staff will be on 9/6 from 6:30-10:30 PM and 9/8 from 12-4 PM. Please check back our Instagram page for details in the upcoming weeks. 
We are also continuing our community service in-person through our community shows, workshops, and outreach. If you're interested specifically in community service, please email our Community Service Chair directly at stimboard@googlegroups.com.

society-for-creative-anachronism.name: Society for Creative Anachronism
society-for-creative-anachronism.description: The University of Pennsylvania's student-run chapter of the Society for Creative Anachronism (SCA), a non-profit volunteer educational organization. The SCA is devoted to the research and re-creation of pre-seventeenth century skills, arts, combat, culture, and employing knowledge of history to enrich the lives of participants through events, demonstrations, and other educational presentations and activities.

muse.name: Wharton Marketing Undergraduate Student Establishment (MUSE)
muse.description:
MUSE, the Marketing Undergraduate Student Establishment, is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania and the 2025 International Platinum AMA chapter. Founded in 2006, MUSE’s mission is to provide students with meaningful professional experience and access to industry resources. Today, the club engages hundreds of students across campus, manages a 1,500-person listserv, and offers opportunities through 8 committees: Generalist Consulting, Social Impact Consulting, Case Team, Internal, External, Conferences, and Digital.
Our GBM Program features monthly meetings and the MUSE Journal, where members write, edit, design, and publish articles on global marketing topics. Beyond publishing, we pride ourselves on the breadth and impact of our work—volunteering in the community, building creative campaigns, designing websites, and consulting for top-tier clients who are consistently impressed by our professionalism.
Join the MUSE family to gain hands-on experience, expand your skills, and connect with peers and industry leaders.
muse.how_to_get_involved:
All committees are recruiting in Fall 2026: Generalist Consulting, Social Impact Practice Consulting, Internal, External, Conferences, Digital Marketing, and Social Impact. Our Case Team competes in the Spring, and so only recruits in the Fall to prepare.
Interested in joining? Make sure to follow us on Instagram to stay updated on our events and check out our website musepenn.org for more information! As a Wharton Council-recognized student organization, MUSE adheres to the University of Pennsylvania Policy on Equal Opportunity. All Penn undergraduates are welcome to sign up to participate in MUSE’s general body membership (GBM) events and programs.

ais.name: Assembly of International Students
ais.description:
The Assembly of International Students is a student group that is run and represented by students of global backgrounds, whether international or not. We organize activities such as the International Student Orientation, mentorship, parties and Phillies games, conferences and alumni networking events, and the Student Ambassador Program. We are also active on campus to promote policy changes within the Penn campus.
We work closely with student government, the university administration, and the Office of International Programs to create tangible benefits for international student life, to magnify the voices of international students at Penn and beyond and to promote collaboration and harmony between students of different nations and culture.
We achieve these aims by advocating for the interests of international students among other student groups, umbrella organizations, and the administration and creating a social network through which international students can connect and utilize in pursuit of common goals and ideals.
ais.how_to_get_involved:
Our Fall applications are open! 
Active committee members are expected to attend weekly committee meetings and complete assigned tasks by committee chairs. They are encouraged to attend all AIS events.

international-business-and-economics-clu.name: Wharton International Business and Economics Club
international-business-and-economics-clu.description: The Wharton International Business and Economics Club (WIBEC) at Penn is a premier undergraduate finance club focusing on the intersection of economics, global affairs, and international relations. Through conversation with industry professionals, analysis of current events, and club workshops, this club aims to provide members with a stronger understanding of how to navigate the world of global business. Individual goals range widely, including preparation for a future career, establishing industry connections, or simply learning where to put capital.
international-business-and-economics-clu.how_to_get_involved:
Join our listserv here:
https://forms.gle/Mhs9f6bY8L96g3AR9
Also check our website for important application and event deadlines:
http://wibec.club/index.html

undergraduate-assembly-ua.name: Undergraduate Assembly (UA)
undergraduate-assembly-ua.description:
About the UA
The Undergraduate Assembly (UA) is the elected, representative body of undergraduates at Penn, charged with improving life for all students through funding, services, and advocacy.
How we work:
We lobby for tangible change at Penn based on student needs
We represent students to administrators and outsiders
We bring students from different groups and identities together 
We provide services to improve student’s quality of life
We fund the other branches of student government and, by extension, all student groups on campus
undergraduate-assembly-ua.how_to_get_involved:
What to learn more about the UA? 
Make sure to check out our website and Instagram. If you're interested in getting involved, fill out our Interest Form to receive u pdates on elections and member applications!
If you have any specific questions, please reach out to our Speaker, Rafaa Bukhary, at speaker@pennua.org. 
Class of 2030:
Welcome to Penn! If you're interested in joining the UA as an elected member, stay tuned to the Penn Student Government website and the NEC's General Election page for updates about election deadlines and information sessions. Information regarding elections for the Fall 2026 semester will be released beginning of the academic year. 
If you do not want to be an elected member, keep reading to learn about how you can still get involved.
Entire Penn Community
